title: Market-data WS protocol & binary framing
body:
## Context
Every live surface in CandleViewer - chart series, footprint, DOM ladder, liquidity heatmap, tape, CVD, order/position state - arrives over **one multiplexed client WebSocket**. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.1 goal 4 makes freezing that transport an R1 objective precisely so R2 (order flow) and R3 (trading) can *add topics* without renegotiating framing, sequencing or backpressure. R1 exit criterion 7 states it bluntly: "WS protocol is frozen: `23-ws-protocol.md` matches the implementation, contract tests pass, and a deliberate breaking change fails CI."

The contract already exists and is normative: `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` (2 689 lines: envelope 3.1, binary format 3.4, lifecycle 4, sub/unsub/ctl 5, topic catalogue 6, snapshot+delta 7, throttling/coalescing/backpressure 8, heartbeats/revocation 9, error catalogue 10, replay 11, JSON Schemas 13-15, conformance matrix 16). This Epic **implements** that document in the API/WS Gateway (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 3.12, module **M23**) and in the web client, and wires the machinery that makes the document and the code provably identical.

The architectural decision is already made in `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0005-ws-protocol-and-binary-encoding.md`: JSON/MessagePack control plane plus a hand-rolled fixed-layout binary data plane, snapshot+delta with per-topic sequence numbers, no checksums. That ADR carries an explicit validation gate ("Spike S5: at least 40% bandwidth reduction and 30% decode-time reduction, else the data plane stays JSON and this ADR is amended") which E17-K01 discharges in this Epic.

Two properties of this Epic are load-bearing for the whole product:
1. **Bounded memory under a slow consumer** (`20-architecture.md` principle P6, protocol goal G4). A backgrounded Electron window must never be able to grow server memory.
2. **Server-authoritative, revocable authorisation** (principle P8, goal G5). A manager must not be able to subscribe to another manager's accounts even by hand-crafting a raw frame.

Story domain: **MKT**. Backend module: **M23** (API/WS Gateway). Train **R1**, sprints **S05-S06**, so that E11/E12 (engine, bar builders) and E16 (recorder) consume a stable transport from the first week of R1.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories covered (MKT domain, transport slice):** US-MKT-005 (live ticker stream: single upstream subscription fanned out, unsubscribe grace, reconnect), US-MKT-006 (tape stream delivery including gap marking to consumers), US-MKT-007 (order-book snapshot+delta, sequence break to resync), US-MKT-003 (batched `ticker` topic for the watchlist: one subscription, at most 10 topics per subscribe frame as the story's NFR demands). US-MKT-001/002/004/008/009 belong to E08/E12 and are **not** re-implemented here; this Epic only carries their data on the wire.

**Engineering (38 pts, Sprints 05-06)**
- **E17-K01** - discharge the ADR-0005 validation gate: measured binary vs JSON bandwidth and decode time on the reference workspace; resolves open items W1 and W2 of `23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.6.
- **E17-T01** - `packages/protocol`: `tools/contracts/extract_ws_schemas.py` producing `ws-schemas.json`, generated Python models and TS types, and the blocking `ws_message_schemas` CI gate.
- **E17-T02** - binary codec: the `CVWB` 24-byte header and body kinds 1-6 (section 3.4), Python encoder plus TypeScript decoder, round-trip property tests and a fuzz corpus.
- **E17-S01** - connection lifecycle: subprotocol negotiation, `hello`/`welcome`/`auth`/`auth_ok`, in-place re-auth, heartbeats, close codes, `bye`-before-close.
- **E17-S02** - `SubscriptionManager`: `sub`/`sub_ok`/`unsub`/`ctl`, the section 6 topic registry and parser, the section 6.3 permission matrix, limits, and mid-connection `revoked`.
- **E17-S03** - `SnapshotService` plus sequencing: per-(connection, topic) sequence domain, `snap`/`d`, the six server-initiated resync triggers, client-initiated `resync` with its rate limit, snapshot chunking above 4 MiB.
- **E17-T03** - `CoalescingQueue` and backpressure: per-family coalescing rules (8.2), adaptive throttle classes (8.3), bounded 8 MiB / 2 000-frame outbound budget and the four-step overflow ladder (8.4).
- **E17-T04** - web client (`apps/web/src/ws`): reconnect with full-jitter backoff, priority resubscription, per-topic gap detection, hidden-tab and off-screen `ctl` throttling, binary decode in a shared worker.
- **E17-T05** - single-source error registry: `tools/errorcodes/generate.py` and the blocking `error_registry_single_source` gate.
- **E17-T06** - observability: `cv_ws_*` metrics, connection-quality spans and the budget #6 assertion.
- **E17-T07** - freeze: reconcile `23-ws-protocol.md` with the implementation, amend ADR-0005 with the measured numbers, add the deliberate-breaking-change CI test.

**Design (8 pts, Sprints 03-06)** - E17-D01 research on how degraded fidelity and disconnection must read to a trader; E17-D02 hi-fi for SCR-152 and CMP-076/077/078/092 with handoff; E17-D03 DES-HEATMAP-01 legibility band; E17-D04 design QA and a11y review of the shipped states.

**QA (12 pts)** - E17-Q01 conformance suite plus black-box plan; E17-Q02 chaos; E17-Q03 k6 load; E17-Q04 E2E, exploratory charter, regression pack and sign-off.

**Security (6 pts)** - E17-X01 STRIDE; E17-X02 review, abuse cases, fuzzing and SAST/DAST rules.

**Screens/components touched:** SCR-152 (disconnected/reconnecting), plus the transport-driven states of SCR-030, SCR-050, SCR-053, SCR-100. Components CMP-076 ConnectionStatus, CMP-077 ReconnectOverlay, CMP-078 StaleDataShade, CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner.

## Out of scope
- **Order entry over WS** - orders/amend/cancel/kill-switch are REST (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`); this Epic carries order *state* only (section 1.2).
- **Bulk history** - windows of bars/footprint/profiles/metrics come from REST `/market/*`.
- **The producers of the data** - Bybit ingestion, book reconstruction and bar building are E08/E12; order-flow engines are E18-E25. This Epic transports whatever those modules publish on the bus.
- **Private topic payload semantics** (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`, `trade_groups`) - the *transport rules* for them (never coalesced, causal ordering S5) are in scope; their content is E29/E34.
- **Replay routing** (`replay_session_id`, section 11) - the `sub` field is accepted and validated here, but the replay clock and session lifecycle are **E26**.
- **Session resumption** - explicitly not in v1 (section 9.3, open item W4).
- Android or any non-web client.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The protocol is frozen and drift is impossible
  Given the implementation is complete
  When CI runs the contracts job
  Then ws_message_schemas, error_registry_single_source and runtime_spec_parity all pass
  And a deliberate breaking change to a frame layout fails the build

Scenario: A trader's workspace attaches and stays correct
  Given an authenticated client subscribes to book.BTCUSDT.50, trades.BTCUSDT, bars.BTCUSDT.time.1 and ticker
  Then each topic delivers a snap before any delta and sequence numbers increase by exactly 1 per frame
  And end-to-end tick-to-pixel latency is under 40 ms p95 locally and backend fan-out add-on is under 20 ms p95

Scenario: A slow consumer cannot hurt the server or other users
  Given a client stops reading its socket for 60 seconds while subscribed to the reference workspace
  Then server memory attributable to that connection never exceeds 8 MiB
  And the documented degradation ladder is followed before the connection is closed with 4429
  And no other connected client observes a sequence gap or latency regression

Scenario: Authorisation is revocable mid-connection
  Given a manager is subscribed to positions for account A
  When the owner withdraws that account grant
  Then a revoked frame naming the account arrives within 1 second and other subscriptions continue untouched

Scenario: Upstream desync never reaches the client as a gap
  Given the upstream Bybit book stream produces a gap in u
  Then the client receives a snap with reason upstream_desync and never a delta applied across the gap
```

## Technical notes / design
Implementation lives in `services/api/app/ws/` per `20-architecture.md` section 3.12: `Handshake` to `SubscriptionManager` to `SnapshotService`/`FeedMultiplexer` to `CoalescingQueue` to `FrameEncoder`. One asyncio TaskGroup per connection with exactly one reader and one writer task (architecture TG5). Bus fan-out is "encode once, send many": a topic's frame is encoded a single time per emission tick and the same buffer is handed to every subscriber, which is what keeps CPU flat in client count.

Config keys (`20-architecture.md` environment table): `CV_MAX_WS_TOPICS_PER_CONN`, plus the limits of section 16.2 surfaced verbatim in `welcome.limits`.

Error codes come exclusively from `23-ws-protocol.md` section 10.2 (28 codes); close codes from section 4.4.

## Test plan
`23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.4 is the master matrix and is implemented across E17-Q01..Q04 and E17-X02: contract (schema parity, binary/structured equivalence, error-catalogue closure), unit (sequence generator, coalescer, book delta application, heatmap bucket selection), integration (upstream gap, revocation, token expiry, replay series), chaos (upstream kill, slow consumer, 5 000 msg/s burst, restart), load (8 connections x 40 symbols x 1 h), E2E (hidden tab, kill-switch), security (query-string token, cross-account subscribe, fuzzed binary bodies). Coverage floor at least 85% on `services/api/app/ws` and `packages/protocol`.

## Security notes
Primary STRIDE areas from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 5: spoofing (first-frame token auth, never in the URL), elevation (topic-to-permission matrix, account-scope narrowing, live revocation), DoS (bounded outbound queue, inbound rate limit, subscription/symbol/connection caps, resync rate limit), tampering (SR-128 bounds-checked binary decode, SR-155 fuzzed decoders). Data classification: market data is internal; private topics are confidential and account-scoped. Security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
The transport itself has no UI, but it *drives* four accessible states: CMP-076 ConnectionStatus (icon plus text plus colour triad, assertive announcement once per state change and not per heartbeat), CMP-077 ReconnectOverlay (`role="alertdialog"`, focus-trapped, non-dismissible), CMP-078 StaleDataShade (visible "Last update Xs ago" text, never opacity alone), CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner. A degraded-fidelity `connection_quality` notice must be announced as `role="status"`, not `alert`, so a lagging connection does not hijack a screen reader mid-trade.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: #3 WS tick to screen p95 under 100 ms and p99 under 250 ms; #6 backend fan-out add-on at most 20 ms p95. From `23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.3: binary book delta decode under 0.15 ms p99; footprint bar (400 cells) under 1.0 ms p99; reference-workspace bandwidth under 350 KiB/s; full re-snapshot under 700 KiB and under 400 ms; upstream_desync resyncs under 1 per hour per topic.

## Observability
`cv_ws_resync_total{reason}`, `cv_ws_overflow_total{reason}`, `cv_ws_clients`, `cv_ws_topics_per_client`, `cv_ws_conflated_total`, per-topic emit latency histogram, connection-quality class gauge. Audit entries for `auth_failed` (warning), slow-consumer close (warning), and every `revoked`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child tickets Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R1 exit criterion 7 demonstrated: doc equals implementation, contract tests green, breaking change fails CI.
- [ ] Budgets #3 and #6 measured and met; section 16.3 client-side budgets recorded.
- [ ] Coverage at least 85% backend/protocol, at least 80% web client.
- [ ] STRIDE finalised and findings triaged; Security engineer sign-off.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-152 and the connection chrome; manual NVDA pass on state announcements.
- [ ] QA epic-level regression and exploratory pass recorded; zero open P0/P1.
- [ ] ADR-0005 amended with measured numbers; `23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.6 open items W1/W2 closed.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
- **E02** - `packages/protocol` codegen scaffold and the monorepo task graph (E02-T09 builds the generator this Epic extends).
- **E04** - metrics facade, correlation-id propagation across WS, latency-budget instrumentation.
- **E08** - Bybit adapter and the internal bus: there is nothing to transport until ingestion publishes normalised events.
- **E09** - auth, sessions and RBAC: the `auth` frame validates the same access tokens and reads the same permission model.
- Consumers: **E11**, **E12**, **E16** in R1; **E21**, **E26** in R2 (roadmap graph edges E17 to E11, E17 to E21).

## Branch
`feat/e17-ws-protocol-epic`; one PR per child ticket, at most 400 LOC diff preferred.

## References
- docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md (the normative contract)
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0005-ws-protocol-and-binary-encoding.md
- docs/plan/20-architecture.md sections 3.12, 4 (P6, P8), 5-7
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md section 5 (R1 scope, exit criteria, quality gates)
- docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md budgets #3, #6
- docs/plan/04-security-program.md section 5, SR-128, SR-155
- docs/plan/11-user-stories.md section 4 MKT
- docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-152; docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md CMP-076..078, CMP-092

## Agent guidance

UI ticket. `E17-S01..S03` and `E17-T04` (web) depend on the contract landed by `E17-T01..T03`; agree the

title: UX research: how a trader must experience a degraded or dropped feed
body:
## Context
The WS protocol has three distinct failure and degradation modes that a trader must be able to tell apart instantly, because each implies a different action:

1. **Stale** - the connection is alive but a topic has not updated for longer than expected (`14-screens-catalogue.md` section 0.5.4: shading after 2 s, last-good timestamp always shown).
2. **Degraded fidelity** - the connection is healthy but the server has classified it `lagging`/`saturated` and is multiplying throttles and forcing coalescing (`23-ws-protocol.md` section 8.3). Data is *correct* but *less frequent*. There is no equivalent in any charting product the Owner currently uses, and it is easy to mis-communicate as "broken".
4. **Disconnected/resyncing** - transport down (SCR-152) or a topic is rebuilding after a sequence gap (SCR-050 has an explicit "Book resynchronising..." state).

Getting this wrong has a trading consequence, not a cosmetic one: a trader who believes a frozen book is live will hit a price that no longer exists, and a trader who abandons a perfectly good chart because a yellow banner looked alarming has lost the trade for no reason. `23-ws-protocol.md` section 10.3 already fixes the *classes* of UI treatment; this research fixes the *vocabulary and prominence* inside those classes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3 moderated sessions (Owner plus up to 2 account managers), 40 minutes, driven by a scripted harness that injects each transport state into a live-looking workspace: stale topic, `connection_quality: saturated`, book resync, full disconnect, planned `shutdown_notice`, `slow_consumer` close.
- Probes: "what just happened?", "is the price on screen safe to trade on?", "what would you do now?", "which of these two states is worse?".
- Competitive scan of how TradingView, Sierra Chart/DeepCharts and the Bybit web terminal signal a stale or degraded feed - specifically whether they distinguish degraded-cadence from disconnected at all.
- Findings in `docs/design/research/e17-feed-states.md`: a ranked severity ordering of the six states, the plain-English label the Owner recognises for each, the minimum prominence each needs, and 5-8 adopted decisions each phrased as a testable statement a wireframe can satisfy or violate.
- A recommendation on the **degraded-fidelity** case in particular: banner, chip, or in-panel only - and whether `coalesced_count` should drive a visible "feed compressed" indicator on the tape-speed widget as `23-ws-protocol.md` section 8.2 suggests.

## Out of scope
- Visual design of any kind - greyscale wireframes begin in E17-D02.
- The recorder's "history starts at ts" empty state (E16) and the ingestion-lag half of CMP-092 (E04).
- Recruiting participants outside the Owner's circle.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every transport state has an evidenced treatment
  When docs/design/research/e17-feed-states.md is reviewed
  Then all six states are listed with a recommended label, prominence and severity rank, each traceable to a specific observation

Scenario: Degraded fidelity is distinguishable from disconnection
  Given participants were shown the saturated-class state and the disconnected state back to back
  Then the report records whether they distinguished them unaided and recommends the treatment that made the distinction reliable

Scenario: A safety misread is caught
  Given a participant treats a stale price as tradeable
  Then the incident is recorded verbatim and drives a decision that raises the prominence of the stale treatment

Scenario: A finding contradicts the catalogue
  Given a finding contradicts 14-screens-catalogue.md section 0.5.4 or 23-ws-protocol.md section 10.3
  Then it is raised as an amendment proposal to that document rather than silently designed around
```

## Technical notes / design
The injection harness is a thin dev-only page driving CMP-076/077/078/092 from a scripted frame log; it does not need the real backend and must not be promoted to production code. Frame scripts are taken verbatim from the worked sessions in `23-ws-protocol.md` section 12 (12.7 slow-consumer degradation then recovery is the key one for the degraded case; 12.3 sequence gap and recovery for the resync case).

## Test plan
N/A (research). Validity control: the same six states are shown in a different order to each participant so ordering does not manufacture the severity ranking.

## Security notes
Session recordings follow `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0015-recording-policy.md`; no real account identifiers, balances or API keys appear in the harness - fixtures only.

## Accessibility notes
At least one session is run with a screen reader active so the announcement policy (assertive once per change for offline/degraded, polite for stale) is validated with a user rather than asserted in a spec.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Report merged at `docs/design/research/e17-feed-states.md` with at least 5 adopted, testable decisions.
- [ ] Severity ranking and labels agreed with the Architect (they constrain 23-ws-protocol.md section 10.3).
- [ ] Findings presented at Design Review; decisions carried into E17-D02 scope.
- [ ] Any contradiction raised as a documented amendment proposal.

## Dependencies
- **E05** design system v0 supplies the tokens and primitives the harness renders with.

## Branch
`design/e17-feed-states-research`

## References
- docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md sections 8.3, 10.3, 12.3, 12.7
- docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md section 0.5.4, SCR-152, SCR-050
- docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md CMP-076, CMP-077, CMP-078, CMP-092
- docs/plan/10-personas.md


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`
2. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`
3. `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`
4. `docs/plan/10-personas.md`

**Repo paths to create/modify**
Base area for `web`: apps/web/src/features/<feature>/ (+ apps/web/src/state, apps/web/src/app/routes as needed)
- 3 moderated sessions (Owner plus up to 2 account managers), 40 minutes, driven by a scripted harness that injects each transport state into a live-looking workspace: stale topic, `connection_quality: saturated`, book resync, full disconnect, planned `shutdown_notice`, `slow_consumer` close.
- Probes: "what just happened?", "is the price on screen safe to trade on?", "what would you do now?", "which of these two states is worse?".
- Competitive scan of how TradingView, Sierra Chart/DeepCharts and the Bybit web terminal signal a stale or degraded feed - specifically whether they distinguish degraded-cadence from disconnected at all.
- Findings in `docs/design/research/e17-feed-states.md`: a ranked severity ordering of the six states, the plain-English label the Owner recognises for each, the minimum prominence each needs, and 5-8 adopted decisions each phrased as a testable statement a wireframe can satisfy or violate.
- A recommendation on the **degraded-fidelity** case in particular: banner, chip, or in-panel only - and whether `coalesced_count` should drive a visible "feed compressed" indicator on the tape-speed widget as `23-ws-protocol.md` section 8.2 suggests.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- None identified beyond internal module boundaries named in Scope / Deliverables above; do not introduce a new public REST/WS surface without a contract-first change (AGENTS.md §3 step 4).

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web build`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/e17-feed-states-research`
- PR title: `E17-D01: UX research: how a trader must experience a degraded or dropped feed`
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder until the issue number is assigned)
- Required reviewers: @CandleViewer/frontend (per `.github/CODEOWNERS` for the touched paths)
- Labels: `type/design`, `area/backend-platform`, `priority/p1`, `design`, `ux-research`

**Done means**
- Report merged at `docs/design/research/e17-feed-states.md` with at least 5 adopted, testable decisions.
- Severity ranking and labels agreed with the Architect (they constrain 23-ws-protocol.md section 10.3).
- Findings presented at Design Review; decisions carried into E17-D02 scope.
- Any contradiction raised as a documented amendment proposal.

**Do NOT**
- Do not implement: Visual design of any kind - greyscale wireframes begin in E17-D02.
- Do not implement: The recorder's "history starts at ts" empty state (E16) and the ingestion-lag half of CMP-092 (E04).
- Do not implement: Recruiting participants outside the Owner's circle.
- Do not hand-edit `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md` (generated from `machines/*.json`).
- Do not create/instantiate a statechart outside `cv.statechart.factory` (ADR-0016).

**If blocked**
- Comment on the GitHub issue naming the exact blocking ticket key or gate (e.g. a failing CI check, an unresolved dependency in `blocked_by`, or a missing upstream decision).
- Move the issue's Status to **Blocked**.
- Never silently work around a failing gate or an unmet dependency — stop and ask (AGENTS.md §3 step 2).

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Design SCR-152 and the connection-state component set to hi-fi with handoff
body:
## Context
E17 is a backend transport Epic with exactly one user-facing surface: the chrome that tells a trader what the transport is doing. That chrome is already enumerated in the catalogues - **SCR-152** (disconnected/reconnecting state, cited by US-MKT-007, US-OBS-004, US-POS-008) and components **CMP-076 ConnectionStatus**, **CMP-077 ReconnectOverlay**, **CMP-078 StaleDataShade**, **CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner** - but none of them has been drawn, and E17-T04 (the web WS client) cannot start until they are signed off (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`).

This ticket takes E17-D01's evidence to wireframes and then hi-fi, and contributes the results back to the design system rather than shipping one-offs in `apps/web`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Wireframes then hi-fi in Figma** for:
  - **SCR-152** full-workspace disconnected/reconnecting state and its **in-panel variant** (SCR-030 chart frozen with last-good timestamp, SCR-050 ladder frozen with click-trading hard-disabled) and its **inline variant** (SCR-001 login "server unreachable").
  - **CMP-076 ConnectionStatus** - all four states (`connected`, `reconnecting`, `degraded`, `offline`) with `lastGoodTs` and optional `latencyMs`, at both TopBar densities.
  - **CMP-077 ReconnectOverlay** - default and retry-exhausted, with the manual "Retry now" affordance and the attempt counter.
  - **CMP-078 StaleDataShade** - fresh and stale, with the mandatory visible "Last update Xs ago" text.

`23-ws-protocol.md` section 6.1.1 resolves former open item W3 by making `heatmap.time_bucket_ms` a **derived** value rather than a constant: a heatmap column should occupy between **2 and 8 device pixels**, with a **3 device-pixel target** encoded as the `/3` divisor in

```
ideal_ms  = (window_seconds * 1000) / (pane_css_width_px * devicePixelRatio / 3)
bucket_ms = smallest allowed value >= ideal_ms from {100, 250, 500, 1000, 5000}
```

plus a normative ladder clamp (never select 5000 when `ideal_ms <= 2500`) and a server fallback of `500` when the option is absent.

The section is explicit about ownership: "the design team owns only the *visual* band (the 2-8 device-pixel legibility range and the 3 px target) and the 'auto' affordance's appearance. The heatmap is a canvas surface and needs an equal-status non-canvas alternative under `05-accessibility-standard.md`; that alternative is E21's scope, but the auto/pinned bucket control designed here must itself be keyboard-reachable and announce its current value.

title: Build the WS protocol conformance suite and the black-box test plan
body:
## Context
`23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.1 states 12 server MUSTs and 12 client MUSTs, and section 16.4 gives a test matrix with named rows. R1 exit criterion 7 requires contract tests to pass as part of declaring the protocol frozen, and `30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.4 makes contract testing an R1 quality gate.

A conformance suite is different from the unit tests inside each story: it treats the gateway as a **black box reachable only through a socket** and asserts the normative requirements directly, by number. That is what makes it reusable - E26 (replay) and every R2 topic addition run the same suite unchanged and find out immediately whether they broke the contract.

This ticket also produces the human-facing black-box test plan required per story group by `03-testing-strategy.md` section 11.1.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Conformance harness** (`tests/conformance/ws/`): a protocol-level client that speaks both `cv.v1.msgpack` and `cv.v1.json`, built on the generated `packages/protocol` types but **not** on `apps/web`'s client - so a bug in the app client cannot mask a server bug.
- **One test per normative requirement**, named for it:
  - **S1** one `sub_ok` result per requested topic, in request order.
  - **S2** `snap` before any `d` on a new subscription unless `snapshot:false` was accepted.
  - **S3** `s` increments by exactly 1 per topic; never reused or skipped (including under concurrent topic writes).
  - **S4** `orders` and `executions` never coalesced or throttled.
  - **S5** causal order `executions` -> `orders` -> `positions` -> `trade_groups`.
  - **S6** outbound queue bounded; never unbounded buffering.
  - **S7** authorisation re-evaluated on grant change with `revoked` emitted.
  - **S8** heuristic payloads tagged `estimated: true`.
  - **S9** replay frames tagged `source: "replay"` / header bit2 with `wt` populated.
  - **S10** only error codes from the section 10.2 catalogue are ever emitted.
  - **S11** `bye` before every server-initiated close.
  - **S12** unknown option keys rejected, not ignored.
- **Contract tests** from section 16.4: every recorded frame validates against its section 13-15 schema; every binary frame decoded then validated against the structured schema (binary/structured equivalence, all six kinds); error-catalogue closure.
- **Named unit-level conformance checks** that belong to the suite rather than to one story: `heatmap_bucket_selection` against every row of the section 6.1.1 reference table plus the ladder clamp and the server's `500` fallback when the option is absent.
- **Integration rows** from section 16.4: upstream `u` gap produces `snap` with `reason: upstream_desync`; grant revocation mid-stream produces `revoked` within 1 s with other topics intact; token expiry produces in-place re-auth preserving subscriptions and sequences; replay subscribe-seek-finish emits the documented frame series (executed against E26 when it lands; until then, asserted against a stubbed replay clock and marked pending).
- **Black-box test plan** in `docs/qa/test-plans/e17-ws-protocol.md` covering the story groups (lifecycle, subscriptions and authorisation, snapshot and resync, backpressure, client behaviour), with per-scenario preconditions, steps, expected results and the section 10.3 UI treatment expected for each error class.
- **Suite wired into CI** as a required check on the `contracts` and `integration` jobs.

## Out of scope
- Chaos (E17-Q02), load (E17-Q03), E2E and exploratory (E17-Q04), security-specific tests (E17-X02).
- Payload *content* correctness (whether a footprint cell has the right volume) - owned by the producing epics; this suite asserts transport contract only.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every normative requirement has a named test
  When the conformance suite is listed
  Then there is at least one test per requirement S1 through S12, named for the requirement it asserts

Scenario: The suite catches a real regression
  Given the sequence generator is deliberately changed to skip a number under concurrency
  Then the S3 test fails

Scenario: Binary and structured are proven equivalent
  Given every binary body kind 1 through 6
  When each is decoded and validated against its structured schema
  Then all pass, and a deliberately corrupted layout fails

Scenario: The error catalogue is closed
  Given a full run exercising every error path
  Then every emitted code appears in section 10.2 and an injected undocumented code fails the suite

Scenario: Heatmap bucket selection is enforced, not aspirational
  Given every row of the 6.1.1 reference table plus the absent-option case
  Then the computed bucket matches the documented value including the 1000 ms ladder clamp

Scenario: The suite runs against both subprotocols
  Then every applicable test passes under cv.v1.msgpack and under cv.v1.json with base64 payloads
```

## Technical notes / design
The harness drives a real server instance from the docker-compose test environment (`03-testing-strategy.md` section 17) fed by **recorded Bybit fixtures** (section 4.1), not live Bybit - so runs are deterministic and consume no rate-limit budget.

Requirement S6 (bounded queue) is asserted here only in its *observable* form (the ladder is followed, the connection is closed rather than growing); the memory measurement itself is E17-Q02's chaos scenario.

Tests are parameterised over the topic registry table from E17-S02, so a topic added in R2 is automatically covered by the generic rows (snapshot-before-delta, sequence monotonicity, option rejection) without anyone remembering to add tests. This is the mechanism that makes the freeze cheap to maintain.

## Test plan
This ticket **is** a test deliverable. Its own quality bar: each test fails when its requirement is deliberately broken - a mutation check run once during review, with the results recorded on the ticket. A conformance test that cannot fail is worse than none.

## Security notes
The suite includes the non-adversarial half of the security matrix (error-catalogue closure, option rejection); the adversarial half - cross-account subscribe, query-string token, fuzzed bodies - is E17-X02, deliberately owned by Security rather than QA.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (protocol level). The section 10.3 UI treatment expectations recorded in the test plan feed E17-Q04's E2E assertions.

The suite must run in under 5 minutes in CI so it can be a required check on every PR; long-running scenarios belong to E17-Q02 and E17-Q03's nightly jobs.

CI output reports the requirement coverage matrix (which of S1-S12 and C1-C12 ran), so a silently skipped requirement is visible rather than green.

title: Build and run the WS chaos scenarios: upstream loss, slow consumer, burst and restart
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` section 9 requires chaos and failover tests, and the planning brief lists them as non-negotiable. For E17 the chaos scenarios are not generic resilience theatre - each one maps to a specific protocol guarantee that is otherwise only asserted on paper:

- Killing the upstream tests **G3** (deterministic correctness under loss): the client must see a snapshot, never a gap.
- A client that stops reading tests **G4** and **P6** (bounded memory): the one property that keeps a sleeping laptop from taking down the backend.
- A 5 000 msg/s burst tests the coalescing design at the ingest rate US-MKT-006 specifies as sustainable.
- A server restart mid-subscription tests the `shutdown_notice` contract that stops a double-send during a deploy.

These are exactly the four chaos rows of `23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.4.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Harness** (`tests/chaos/ws/`) with deterministic fault injection: a network proxy (toxiproxy-style) between the gateway and its clients and between ingestion and the recorded-fixture upstream, plus process-level controls for restart.
- **Scenario 1 - upstream kill**: kill the upstream public WS mid-stream; assert a `snap` with `reason: upstream_desync` or `upstream_reconnect` on every affected topic, **no gap ever delivered to a client**, `cv_ws_resync_total{reason}` increments, and the client's book after recovery equals the server's.
- **Scenario 2 - slow consumer**: a client stops reading for 60 s while subscribed to the reference workspace; assert at every budget check that the connection's accounted bytes and frames stay within the 8 MiB / 2 000-frame budget (`23-ws-protocol.md` §8.4 and §8.6 name the bounded overshoots), and record the tracemalloc peak with its ratio to the accounted bytes on the ticket (ruling D8), the degradation order of section 8.4 is followed step by step, a `4429` close occurs only when what remains cannot be dropped or a topic's snapshot is re-dropped three times (`23-ws-protocol.md` §8.4 step 3), the `bye` names `most_expensive_topics`, and **no other connected client sees a sequence gap or a latency regression**.
- **Scenario 3 - burst**: 5 000 msg/s on one symbol; assert coalescing engages with `coalesced_count` above 1, **no sequence break**, fan-out p95 stays inside budget #6, and per-symbol isolation holds - the other nine symbols' latency is unaffected (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 9's isolation clause).
- **Scenario 4 - server restart**: restart the gateway during active subscriptions; assert `shutdown_notice` is broadcast on `system` with `closing_in_ms` and `expected_downtime_ms`, a clean `1001` close follows after the grace period, the client reconnects with jittered backoff and resubscribes in priority order, and order-entry affordances were disabled for the duration.

```gherkin
  Given 5000 messages per second on one symbol for 60 seconds
  Then frames carry coalesced true with coalesced_count above 1, no sequence number is skipped
  And the other nine symbols' fan-out p95 stays within budget

Scenario: Restart is announced before it happens
  Given the gateway is restarted during active subscriptions
  Then shutdown_notice precedes the close, the close code is 1001, and the client resubscribes in the documented priority order

Scenario: Token expiry during an outage recovers
  Given the token expires while the client is disconnected and backing off
  Then the client refreshes over REST before reconnecting and does not loop on 4401

Scenario: A revoked account is not resurrected by resubscription

```

Load runs use fixture data on a staging environment with no live keys and no live account state. k6 scripts must not embed a real token; they authenticate against a staging identity provisioned for the purpose.

The whole ticket. Budgets asserted: #3, #6 from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; frame decode, bandwidth, re-snapshot size and duration, resync rate from `23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.3.

title: E2E suite, exploratory charter, regression pack and QA sign-off for E17
body:
## Context
The conformance suite proves the server obeys the contract and the chaos suite proves it survives; neither proves that **a trader sitting in front of the app has a correct and honest experience** when the transport misbehaves. `03-testing-strategy.md` sections 7, 11.2 and 16 require E2E suites, an exploratory charter and an explicit QA sign-off before "In Test" can close, and `30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.4 names Playwright web **and** Electron as an R1 gate.

This ticket closes E17 from the user's side and produces the regression pack that every later train runs.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Playwright E2E additions** (web and Electron), including the two rows section 16.4 names explicitly:
  - **Hidden tab drops throttles; a restored tab does not re-snapshot** (client obligation C8).
  - **A kill-switch frame disables the order ticket without a REST round-trip** (C12).
  Plus: cold start of a 4-pane workspace reaching data on every pane; symbol switch without a socket reconnect; disconnect shows SCR-152 and reconnect restores all panes with fresh snapshots; a forced sequence gap shows the resyncing state and then correct data; a slow-consumer close shows the capacity toast advising fewer panes; a `shutdown_notice` shows a countdown and disables order entry; a `revoked` on a private topic shows the withdrawal message while other panes keep streaming.
- **Exploratory charters** (`03-testing-strategy.md` section 11.2), timeboxed 90 minutes each, with session notes: (1) "break the client's state by racing pane open/close against reconnects"; (2) "find a state where the UI shows data that is not actually current"; (3) "find a combination of throttles and pane visibility that produces a wrong or frozen render". Charter 2 is the highest-value one and is run by the QA lead personally, because a silently stale price is the failure mode with real money attached.
- **Accessibility audit** of the E17 surface: axe-core on SCR-152 and the chrome in every transport state, manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes over the state transitions, keyboard operation of the reconnect overlay, `prefers-reduced-motion`, and 200% zoom reflow. Cross-checked against E17-D04's design-QA findings so the two passes do not duplicate or, worse, each assume the other covered it.
- **Regression pack**: the stable subset of the E2E scenarios tagged for the release regression suite so every later train re-runs E17's guarantees; registered in the regression pack index.
- **Traceability**: the matrix template of `03-testing-strategy.md` section 18 completed for US-MKT-003, US-MKT-005, US-MKT-006 and US-MKT-007 (transport slice), mapping each story's acceptance criteria to the tests that cover them.
- **QA sign-off** per `03-testing-strategy.md` section 16, recorded on the Epic.

## Out of scope
- Protocol-level conformance (E17-Q01), chaos (E17-Q02), load (E17-Q03), adversarial security (E17-X02).
- Chart rendering correctness (E11/E12) beyond "the pane shows data that matches the feed".
- Order placement flows (E29-E34) - only the kill-switch and shutdown gating of the ticket's *affordances* is in scope here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The named E2E rows pass on both shells
  Given the Playwright suite runs on web and on Electron
  Then the hidden-tab and kill-switch scenarios pass on both

Scenario: A trader is never shown stale data as live

Scenario: Exploratory findings are dispositioned
  Given the three charters are executed
  Then every finding is filed with the standard taxonomy and severity, and no P0 or P1 remains open at sign-off

Scenario: Sign-off is evidenced
  Then the sign-off comment lists the suites run, the coverage achieved, the open defects by severity and an explicit accept or reject
```

## Technical notes / design
E2E drives transport states through E17-T04's dev-only fault-injection channel plus the chaos proxy, so scenarios are deterministic rather than timing-dependent - the usual cause of flaky transport E2E. Flake policy per section 14: quarantine within a day, fix or replace, never retry into green.

Electron coverage is not optional: the hidden-window throttling path differs between a browser tab and an Electron `BrowserWindow`, and Electron is the primary shell.

The traceability matrix is generated from test annotations rather than maintained by hand, so it cannot silently rot.

This ticket is a test deliverable. Coverage expectation for the E17 web client is at least 80% (frontend floor); the E2E suite is a required check on the `e2e` job, with the full set nightly and the tagged smoke subset per PR.

Exploratory charter 2 ("find a state where the UI shows data that is not actually current") doubles as a safety review: any finding there is triaged as at least P1 regardless of how obscure the reproduction is, because the consequence is a trade on a false price. Test identities are staging users; no live keys or accounts are used.

The audit described above is a hard gate: `30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.4 requires axe-core zero violations on all R1 routes plus a manual NVDA and VoiceOver pass. Transcripts are attached to the ticket as evidence, not summarised.

E2E asserts the perceptible budgets rather than the microscopic ones: stale treatment appears within 2 s of the last expected update; reconnect restores panes within 10 s; the chrome's 1 Hz updates do not re-render the workspace subtree (React profiler trace attached).

Each E2E run publishes its pass/fail and duration to the CI dashboard; the regression pack's results are part of the R1 PRR evidence bundle.

title: Implement the WS connection lifecycle: negotiation, auth handshake, in-place re-auth and heartbeats
body:
## Context
Before a single market-data frame can flow, a connection must negotiate a subprotocol, identify itself, authenticate, and agree the limits it will be held to. `23-ws-protocol.md` section 4 specifies that lifecycle as a state machine, and two of its properties are non-obvious and load-bearing:

- **Auth is a first frame, not a header or a query string.** Browser WebSockets cannot set headers, and a token in the URL "would land in proxy logs and browser history" (section 4.3). So the socket opens unauthenticated and accepts only `auth` and `ping` until `auth_ok`.
- **Re-authentication happens in place.** When the access token nears expiry the client refreshes over REST and sends a new `auth` frame on the *same* socket; subscriptions, sequence numbers and book state all survive. Without this, every 10-minute token refresh would force a full re-snapshot of the whole workspace.

This story delivers US-MKT-005's reconnect clause ("the socket drops, it reconnects with exponential backoff and re-subscribes, and consumers see a brief reconnecting state rather than stale values") on the server side; the client side is E17-T04.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Endpoint** `wss://<host>/api/v1/ws` in `services/api/app/ws/`, same origin, same TLS termination and same Tailscale-only exposure as REST; plain `ws://` accepted on loopback only.
- **Subprotocol negotiation** (section 2.2): accept `cv.v1.msgpack` (preferred) and `cv.v1.json`, echo exactly one, close `1002` before the handshake completes when neither is offered. Enable `permessage-deflate` for `cv.v1.json` and **disable** it for `cv.v1.msgpack` (section 3.5).
- **`hello` -> `welcome`** (section 4.2): reject any non-`hello` first frame with `1002`; reply with `protocol`, `encoding`, `server_version`, `git_sha`, `connection_id`, `server_time_ms`, `clock_skew_ms` (server time minus the client's `clock_ms`), `auth_required`, `auth_timeout_ms`, `heartbeat` policy and the full `limits` block of section 16.2 (`max_subscriptions` 200, `max_topics_per_request` 50, `max_inbound_frame_bytes` 262144, `max_outbound_frame_bytes` 4194304, `min_throttle_ms` 50, `max_symbols_per_connection` 40) and `features`.
- **`auth` -> `auth_ok`** (section 4.3): validate the bearer access token against E09's session service; reply with `user_id`, `username`, `roles`, `permissions`, `account_scope`, `allowed_environments`, `session_id`, `token_expires_at_ms` and current `kill_switch` state. Until `auth_ok` only `auth` and `ping` are accepted; anything else yields `not_authenticated` and closes after 3 such frames. `auth_timeout_ms` 10 s without success yields `bye` `auth_timeout` and close `4401`; 3 failed attempts yields `bye` `auth_failed`, close `4401` and a `warning` audit entry.
- **In-place re-auth** (section 4.1): a second `auth` on an authenticated socket re-validates and updates identity **without** touching subscriptions or sequence counters. Token expiry without re-auth yields `bye` `token_expired` and close `4401`.
- **Implicit `system` subscription** at `auth_ok` (section 6.2), which the client may not unsubscribe.
- **Heartbeats** (section 9.1): server replies `pong` echoing `id` and including its clock; server sends unsolicited `ping` after 20 s of silence; either side seeing no traffic for `heartbeat.timeout_ms` (45 s) closes.
- **Inbound limits**: max inbound frame 256 KiB -> close `1009`; client inbound rate 30 frames/s and 300/min excluding `pong` -> `client_rate_limited` then close `4429`.
- **Close codes and `bye`** (section 4.4): `bye` is always sent *before* the close frame with a machine-readable reason, `retry_after_ms` where applicable and `reconnect` boolean. Implement `1000`, `1001`, `1002`, `1009`, `1011`, `1013`, `4401`, `4403`, `4429`, `4400`.
- **Planned shutdown** (section 9.4): broadcast `shutdown_notice` on `system` with `closing_in_ms` and `expected_downtime_ms`, then close `1001` after a 5 s grace period, wired into the application's shutdown sequence (`20-architecture.md` start/stop order: gateway stops first).
- **Max connections per user 8**: closing the oldest idle connection with `bye` when exceeded.
- **Per-connection TaskGroup**: exactly one reader and one writer task (`20-architecture.md` TG5), with correlated `request_id` propagation into E04's logging context.

## Out of scope
- Subscriptions and topic authorisation (E17-S02) - this story ends at an authenticated, heartbeating socket with `system` attached.
- Snapshot and sequencing (E17-S03), coalescing and backpressure (E17-T03).
- Token issuance, refresh, MFA and the session store - **E09** owns those; this story consumes them.
- The client-side reconnect strategy (E17-T04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Happy-path handshake
  Given a client connects offering cv.v1.msgpack and cv.v1.json
  When it sends hello then auth with a valid access token
  Then the server echoes cv.v1.msgpack, replies welcome with the full limits block, replies auth_ok with roles, permissions and account_scope
  And the connection is implicitly subscribed to system

Scenario: No mutually supported subprotocol
  Given a client offers only a subprotocol the server does not know
  Then the connection is closed with 1002 before the handshake completes

Scenario: Anything before hello is a protocol error
  Given a connected client sends sub as its first frame
  Then the server closes with 1002

Scenario: Token in the query string is refused
  Given a client connects with an access token in the URL query string and sends no auth frame
  Then the token is ignored, the auth timeout fires after 10 seconds, and bye with auth_timeout and close 4401 follow

Scenario: Three failed auth attempts
  Given a client sends three auth frames with invalid tokens
  Then the third is answered with bye auth_failed and close 4401, and a warning audit entry is written

Scenario: Re-auth preserves everything
  Given an authenticated connection with active subscriptions at sequence 5000 on a topic
  When the client sends a fresh auth frame with a refreshed token
  Then auth_ok is returned, no snapshot is emitted, subscriptions remain, and the next delta on that topic carries sequence 5001

Scenario: Token expires without re-auth
  Given token_expires_at_ms passes with no new auth frame
  Then the server sends bye token_expired and closes 4401 rather than continuing to serve an expired identity

Scenario: Heartbeat timeout
  Given a client stops sending anything for 45 seconds
  Then the server closes the connection

Scenario: Inbound rate limit
  Given a client sends 40 non-pong frames in one second
  Then it receives err client_rate_limited and, on continued violation, bye and close 4429

Scenario: Planned shutdown is announced
  Given the process receives a shutdown signal
  Then a shutdown_notice is broadcast on system with closing_in_ms 5000 and expected_downtime_ms, and the socket closes 1001 after the grace period
```

## Technical notes / design
State machine implemented explicitly (section 4.1): `Connecting -> Negotiated -> HelloSent -> AwaitingAuth -> Authenticated -> Subscribed`, with `Reauthenticating` looping back to `Authenticated` and `Closing` reachable from everywhere. An explicit enum and transition table, not implicit boolean flags - the conformance tests of E17-Q01 assert transitions directly.

`clock_skew_ms` is reported, never corrected server-side; the UI warns above plus or minus 2 000 ms because a skewed client mis-renders bar-close countdowns.

Auth validates against E09's token verifier and resolves permissions and `account_scope` through the same RBAC service REST uses - there must be exactly one authorisation source, not a WS copy of the rules.

`bye` payloads carry `code`, `reason`, `message`, `retry_after_ms`, `reconnect` per section 4.4's example. Every server-initiated close goes through one `close_with(reason)` helper so requirement S11 ("send `bye` before every server-initiated close") is structurally guaranteed rather than remembered.

Config: `CV_WS_AUTH_TIMEOUT_MS` (10000), `CV_WS_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS` (15000), `CV_WS_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS` (45000), `CV_WS_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_USER` (8).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: transition table exhaustively (every state x every frame type, including illegal pairs); `clock_skew_ms` arithmetic; `bye`-before-close helper; rate-limit counter window behaviour at the boundary.
- **Integration**: full handshake over a real socket for both subprotocols; auth timeout; 3 failed attempts plus audit entry; **in-place re-auth preserves subscriptions and sequences** (section 16.4 names this explicitly); token expiry; heartbeat timeout in both directions; oversize inbound frame closes `1009`; 9th connection for one user closes the oldest idle one.
- **Contract**: `hello`, `welcome`, `auth`, `auth_ok`, `ping`, `pong`, `bye` frames validate against the section 13 schemas.
- **Security**: token in query string rejected; expired token closes `4401` (both named in section 16.4).
- Coverage target: at least 85%.

## Security notes
Threats (`04-security-program.md` section 5): **spoofing** - token presented in-band on an already-open socket, so the auth window is a documented, bounded, audited 10 s with a 3-attempt cap; **information disclosure** - the token must never appear in a URL, an access log, a metric label or an error message, and this is asserted by test; **DoS** - unauthenticated sockets are cheap and short-lived by construction (10 s timeout, 8-connection cap, inbound rate limit before auth as well as after). `auth_failed` and slow-consumer closes write `warning` audit entries. Data classification: `auth_ok` payload is confidential (names the user's account scope). **Security review label required.**

## Accessibility notes
No direct UI. The `shutdown_notice` this story emits drives the countdown designed in E17-D02, and critically drives **disabling the order ticket** during the grace period (client rule C12) - the payload must therefore always carry `expected_downtime_ms` so the UI can show a countdown instead of a bare "disconnected".

## Performance notes
Handshake to `auth_ok` under 50 ms p95 excluding network. Heartbeat handling must not allocate per beat at 8 connections x 15 s. The per-connection reader/writer task pair is the unit of isolation: one connection's slow auth must not delay another's frames.

## Observability
`cv_ws_clients` gauge; `cv_ws_handshake_seconds` histogram; `cv_ws_auth_failures_total{reason}`; `cv_ws_closes_total{code,reason}`; `cv_ws_clock_skew_ms` histogram. Every connection logs `connection_id`, `user_id`, `session_id` and the negotiated subprotocol at INFO with E04's correlation id; audit events `ws.auth.failure` and `ws.connection.closed{reason}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated and green.
- [ ] Contract tests pass for every control frame in this story's scope.
- [ ] Coverage at least 85% on the lifecycle module.
- [ ] Security review recorded; query-string-token and expired-token tests present.
- [ ] Metrics and audit events emitted and visible on E04's dashboards.
- [ ] `23-ws-protocol.md` section 4 reconciled with the implementation.
- [ ] Two approvals including one code-owner; merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E17-T01** - generated control-frame models and the schema gate.
- **E09** - token verification, session store, RBAC permission and account-scope resolution, audit writer.
- **E04** - correlation ids and the metrics facade.

title: Implement subscriptions, the topic registry, per-topic authorisation and live revocation
body:
## Context
This is the control plane a trader's workspace actually talks to: a four-pane chart layout opens and closes topics constantly as panes mount, symbols change, panes scroll out of view and tabs are backgrounded. `23-ws-protocol.md` section 5.4 is explicit about why `ctl` exists rather than unsub/sub: "a pane that scrolls out of view drops to 1 000 ms, a maximised DOM goes to 20 ms, a backgrounded Electron window goes to 1 000 ms for everything. Doing that with unsub/sub would re-snapshot a 200-level book every time the user switches tabs."

It is also where **authorisation** lives. `20-architecture.md` principle P8 and protocol goal G5 require authorisation to be server-authoritative and revocable mid-connection: a manager must not reach another manager's accounts even by hand-crafting a raw frame, and withdrawing a grant must terminate the affected subscriptions *visibly* (`revoked`) rather than silently emptying them, "which would look like a flat book or a closed position".

Covers US-MKT-005 (single upstream subscription fanned out to all consumers; unsubscribe after a 30-second grace period when the last consumer closes) and US-MKT-003's NFR (one batched `ticker` subscription for the whole watchlist, at most 10 topics per subscribe frame).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Topic registry and parser** for the full section 6 catalogue. Public: `book.{symbol}.{depth}` (depth in {1,50,200,500} in the *name*), `trades.{symbol}`, `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`, `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`, `heatmap.{symbol}`, `profile.{symbol}.{kind}`, `metrics.{symbol}`, `ticker.{symbol}`, `ticker` (batched, `symbols` at most 40), `liquidations.{symbol}`, `liquidations`. Private: `orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`, `trade_groups`, `rules`, `alerts`, `recorder`, `system`. Parsing rules: dots are illegal inside `param`; `atr:14` and `10:3` use a colon; an unknown family yields `unknown_topic`, a malformed string yields `invalid_topic_format`, a non-USDT-linear-perp symbol yields `unsupported_symbol`.
- **`sub` handling** (section 5.1): per-topic `opts`, `snapshot` flag, `replay_session_id` accepted and validated (routing is E26). **Unknown option keys are rejected, never ignored** (requirement S12) so typos surface immediately. Universal options `throttle_ms` (floored at 50), `encoding` (`binary`|`structured`, `encoding_unsupported` when the topic has no binary form), `coalesce`.
- **`sub_ok`** (section 5.2): exactly one result per requested topic, **in request order** (requirement S1); partial success is normal - one bad topic never fails the batch; every ok result carries `sub_id`, `snapshot_pending` and an `effective` block echoing the options **after clamping**.
- **`unsub` / `unsub_ok`** (section 5.3): idempotent - unsubscribing from an unknown or already-removed topic returns `ok: true, noop: true`, because pane-close races are normal.
- **`ctl` / `ctl_ok`** (section 5.4): retune `throttle_ms` live without re-snapshot; changing `depth`, `price_grouping`, `bar_type`/`param`, `time_bucket_ms` or the `metrics` list answers `ctl_ok` with `resnapshot: true` and triggers a fresh `snap` (the emission itself is E17-S03). `ctl` on an unsubscribed topic yields `not_subscribed`.
- **Permission matrix** (section 6.3): `marketdata:read` for all public families; `orders:read` for `orders`/`trade_groups`; `positions:read`; `executions:read`; `accounts:read` for `wallet`; `rules:read`; `alerts:read` (own alerts only); `recording:read`; `system` implicit and role-filtered. Missing permission yields `forbidden`.
- **Account-scope narrowing** (section 6.2): intersect requested `exchange_account_ids` with the caller's grants and **silently narrow**, reporting the effective list in `sub_ok.effective`; requesting *only* out-of-scope accounts yields `account_scope_denied`.
- **Live revocation** (section 9.5, requirement S7): re-evaluate authorisation on every change to roles, permissions, account grants and on kill-switch transitions; terminate affected subscriptions with a `revoked` frame carrying `reason` from the closed set (`permission_revoked`, `account_scope_changed`, `user_disabled`, `session_revoked`, `key_revoked`, `account_disabled`, `replay_session_ended`, `resync_rate_limited`, `topic_removed`), `removed_accounts` where applicable and `resubscribe_allowed`. A fully disabled user gets `bye` and close `4403`.
- **Limits** (section 16.2): 200 subscriptions per connection (`subscription_limit`), 50 topics per `sub` frame (`too_many_topics`), 40 symbols per connection, duplicate subscribe yields `duplicate_subscription` with the advice to use `ctl`.
- **Upstream reference counting** (US-MKT-005): one upstream subscription per (symbol, topic) regardless of how many connections or panes want it; when the last consumer unsubscribes, the upstream subscription is dropped after a **30-second grace period**, so a pane close followed by a reopen does not churn the exchange connection.
- **Replay coexistence** (section 11): a live and a replay subscription to the same topic name coexist, disambiguated by `sub_id`, with replay frames carrying `rs`. Private topics with a `replay_session_id` are rejected with `invalid_options`.

## Out of scope
- Emitting snapshots and deltas, sequencing and resync (E17-S03).
- Coalescing, adaptive throttling and backpressure (E17-T03) - this story clamps and records the *requested* values; enforcement of cadence is there.
- The replay clock and session lifecycle (E26).
- The content of any payload - produced by E08/E12/E18-E25/E29.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Partial success is normal
  Given a sub frame requesting book.BTCUSDT.50, trades.BTCUSDT and orders for an out-of-scope account
  Then sub_ok returns three results in request order, the first two ok with sub_id and effective, the third failing with account_scope_denied
  And the two accepted subscriptions are active

Scenario: Clamping is reported, not silent
  Given a client requests throttle_ms 5 on book.BTCUSDT.50
  Then sub_ok effective reports throttle_ms 50 so the client stops expecting 200 frames per second

Scenario: An unknown option is an error, not a shrug
  Given a client subscribes to footprint.BTCUSDT.time.5 with an option key min_stak
  Then the topic is rejected with invalid_options naming the field, and no subscription is created

Scenario: Malformed topic names are distinguished
  Given the topics book.BTCUSDT.77, bars.BTCUSDT.time.1.5 and book.ETHUSD.50
  Then they are rejected with invalid_topic_format, invalid_topic_format and unsupported_symbol respectively

Scenario: Teardown is idempotent
  Given a pane closes twice in a race and unsubscribes book.BTCUSDT.50 twice
  Then both unsub_ok results are ok true, the second carrying noop true, and no error is raised

Scenario: ctl retunes without re-snapshot
  Given an active book.BTCUSDT.50 subscription at sequence 3000
  When the client sends ctl with throttle_ms 200
  Then ctl_ok reports effective throttle_ms 200, resnapshot is absent or false, and the sequence continues from 3001

Scenario: ctl that changes state identity forces a re-snapshot
  Given an active heatmap.BTCUSDT subscription
  When the client sends ctl with time_bucket_ms 1000
  Then ctl_ok carries resnapshot true and a fresh snap follows

Scenario: A manager cannot reach another manager's accounts by raw frame
  Given a manager whose scope contains only account A
  When it sends a hand-crafted sub for positions with exchange_account_ids [B]
  Then the topic is rejected with account_scope_denied and no positions data is ever emitted for B

Scenario: Grants withdrawn mid-stream are announced
  Given a manager is subscribed to positions for accounts A and B
  When the owner withdraws account B
  Then a revoked frame arrives within 1 second with reason account_scope_changed and removed_accounts [B]
  And the subscription for A and all other topics continue uninterrupted

Scenario: Limits are enforced
  Given a connection holding 200 subscriptions
  When it subscribes to one more
  Then the request is rejected with subscription_limit and the existing subscriptions are untouched

Scenario: The upstream is shared and not churned
  Given three panes across two connections all view book.BTCUSDT.50
  Then exactly one upstream Bybit subscription exists
  And when the last of them closes, the upstream subscription is dropped only after a 30-second grace period

Scenario: system cannot be unsubscribed
  Given an authenticated connection
  When it sends unsub for system
  Then the request is refused and the connection remains subscribed
```

## Technical notes / design
`SubscriptionManager` holds per-connection state: `{sub_id -> Subscription{topic, opts_effective, seq, class, replay_session_id}}`, plus reverse indexes by topic and by account so a grant change resolves affected subscriptions in O(affected) rather than scanning every connection.

The topic registry is **data, not code branches**: one declarative table per family giving the name pattern, the option schema (with types, ranges and defaults), the required permission, the scope-narrowing rule, the default throttle, whether a binary form exists, and the payload schema `$id`. `sub_ok.effective`, the error messages and the E17-Q01 conformance tests are all generated from that table, so adding a topic in R2 (footprint, heatmap, profile, metrics already listed; detectors added later) is a table entry, not a new code path. This is the concrete mechanism behind the R1 goal "freeze the WS protocol so R2/R3 add topics without renegotiating transport".

Authorisation is evaluated by calling E09's RBAC service - never by a local copy of the rules. Revocation is driven by subscribing to E09's grant-change and kill-switch events on the internal bus; the handler must complete within 1 s for the acceptance criterion to hold, so it resolves affected subscriptions from the reverse index and enqueues `revoked` frames ahead of data frames.

Upstream reference counting is keyed by (symbol, family, params) across *all* connections, with a 30 s `asyncio` timer cancelled on re-subscription.

Errors: `unknown_topic`, `invalid_topic_format`, `unsupported_symbol`, `invalid_options`, `encoding_unsupported`, `forbidden`, `account_scope_denied`, `subscription_limit`, `too_many_topics`, `duplicate_subscription`, `not_subscribed` - all from section 10.2, none invented (requirement S10).

- **Unit**: topic parser over a table of valid and invalid names covering every family, depth enum, bar-type/param colon forms, and dotted-param rejection; option validation per family including boundary values (`min_stack` 2 and 10, `throttle_ms` 5/50/1000, `symbols` 40 and 41); permission matrix as a role x topic fixture matrix; scope-narrowing intersection including the empty-intersection case.

- **Contract**: `sub`, `sub_ok`, `unsub`, `unsub_ok`, `ctl`, `ctl_ok`, `revoked`, `err` validate against section 13.5-13.6 schemas; no emitted error code lies outside section 10.2.
- **Security**: cross-account raw-frame subscribe denied; viewer subscribing to `orders` succeeds read-only.
- Coverage target: at least 85%.

## Security notes
This is the Epic's primary **elevation-of-privilege** surface (`04-security-program.md` section 5). title: Implement snapshot+delta sequencing, resync triggers and snapshot chunking
body:
## Context
This story delivers protocol goal **G3**: "Correctness under loss is deterministic, not best-effort." Bybit provides no checksum on its book stream (research digest 06 section 19), so the only correct recovery from any doubt is drop-and-rebuild. `23-ws-protocol.md` section 7 turns that into a contract with exactly three server guarantees and three client obligations, and section 3.3 explains why the sequence number is **ours**, on the envelope, and not Bybit's `u`/`seq`: gap detection must be uniform across every topic including derived ones Bybit has no sequence for (footprint, metrics, heatmap), and a coalesced delta must consume exactly one sequence number so that "no gap" always means "no loss of *state*".

This is the story that makes US-MKT-007 true end to end - "given the update sequence is not contiguous, the book is invalidated, a fresh snapshot is requested and dependent views show resyncing for that interval" - and US-MKT-006's gap clause for the tape.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **`SnapshotService`**: build initial state per topic from the owning module (book engine for `book`, bar builder for `bars`, order-flow engines for `footprint`/`heatmap`/`profile`/`metrics`, ticker cache, OMS for private topics), rendered in binary (kinds 1, 3, 4, 5, 6) or structured per the subscription's `encoding`.
- **Per-(connection, topic) sequence domain** (requirement S3): `s` starts at the `snap`'s value and increments by **exactly 1** per delivered frame; never reused, never skipped, correct under concurrent writes to different topics on one connection.
- **Frame ordering guarantees**: a `snap` precedes any `d` on a newly subscribed topic unless `snapshot: false` was accepted (S2); causal order preserved across private topics `executions -> orders -> positions -> trade_groups` (S5).
- **Universal snapshot payload fields** (section 7.2): `price_scale`, `qty_scale`, `stale`, `estimated`, `source` (`live`|`replay`) on every `snap`, for every topic.
- **Delta semantics** (section 7.3): size `"0"` removes a level; an unmentioned level is unchanged; levels leaving the subscribed depth window are emitted with size 0 so the client's window stays exactly `depth` levels per side.
- **Server-initiated resync** (section 7.4) on all six triggers, each carrying `meta.reason` and `meta.previous_seq`: `upstream_desync` (gap in Bybit's `u`), `upstream_reconnect`, `backpressure` (raised by E17-T03), `reconfigure` (a state-identity-changing `ctl` from E17-S02), `instrument_revision` (tick-size change invalidates the scales in prior frames), `replay_seek` (E26 raises it). Plus `initial` and `client_resync` as the two non-incident reasons.
- **Client-initiated `resync`** (section 7.5): answered with a `snap` correlated by `ch`; rate limited to **5 per topic per minute**, after which `err resync_rate_limited` is returned and the subscription is closed with `revoked` - "a client resyncing in a tight loop is broken and is consuming snapshot-build cost that harms every other consumer".
- **Attaching without a snapshot** (section 7.6): accept `snapshot: false` with `from_seq`/`from_ts_ms` **only** when continuity can be proven (state covering `from_ts_ms` is held and no resync occurred since); otherwise answer `sub_ok` with `snapshot_forced: true` and send a `snap` anyway.
- **Snapshot chunking** (section 3.6): a `snap` exceeding the 4 MiB outbound frame limit is split into N frames sharing one `id`, each with the binary header `partial` flag (bit3) set and the last one clearing it; **all chunks consume one sequence number in total**, assigned to the final chunk, with intermediate chunks carrying `s: null`.
- **Heatmap snapshot cap** (section 6.1.1): the most recent **2 000 columns** at any bucket size; older columns are served by REST `GET /market/heatmap` on scroll-back.
- **Freshness flag**: `stale: true` when the backend's own upstream feed is behind its freshness SLO, so the UI can raise CMP-078 rather than present a frozen value as live.

## Out of scope
- Coalescing, throttling, adaptive classes and the backpressure overflow ladder (E17-T03) - this story emits frames; that one decides when and how many.
- Producing the underlying state: book reconstruction (E08), bar building (E12), order-flow aggregates (E18-E25), OMS state (E29).
- Replay clock and seek (E26) - this story implements the `replay_seek` resync reason and the `source: "replay"` tagging, driven by E26's events.
- REST heatmap scroll-back (E21).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Snapshot precedes deltas and the sequence is unbroken
  Given a client subscribes to book.BTCUSDT.50 with snapshot true
  Then the first data frame is a snap carrying the full 50-level book on each side, price_scale, qty_scale, stale, estimated and source
  And every subsequent delta increments s by exactly 1

Scenario: Applying deltas reproduces server state exactly
  Given a snapshot and 10 000 subsequent deltas from a recorded fixture
  When they are applied in order by a reference client
  Then the resulting book is identical to the server's book at that point, including deletions at size 0 and depth-window evictions

Scenario: Upstream desync produces a snapshot, never a gap
  Given the upstream Bybit book stream skips an update id
  Then the server emits a snap with meta.reason upstream_desync and meta.previous_seq
  And no client ever receives a delta that would be applied across the upstream gap
  And cv_ws_resync_total{reason="upstream_desync"} increments

Scenario: A client resyncing in a loop is stopped
  Given a client sends 6 resync frames for one topic within a minute
  Then the sixth is answered with err resync_rate_limited and the subscription is closed with revoked

Scenario: A state-identity change re-snapshots
  Given an active book.BTCUSDT.50 subscription
  When the instrument's tick size is revised
  Then a snap with reason instrument_revision is emitted and the new price_scale applies from that frame onwards

Scenario: Large snapshots are chunked, not truncated
  Given a footprint snapshot whose encoded size exceeds 4 MiB
  Then it is delivered as N frames sharing one id, each with the partial flag set except the last
  And the chunks consume exactly one sequence number in total, assigned to the final chunk

Scenario: Attaching without a snapshot is only allowed when provable
  Given a client subscribes with snapshot false and a from_ts_ms the server no longer covers
  Then sub_ok reports snapshot_forced true and a snap is sent anyway

Scenario: Private topic causal order holds
  Given a fill arrives that closes a position and completes a trade group
  Then the client receives executions before orders before positions before trade_groups

Scenario: Coalescing does not look like loss
  Given 50 book updates are merged into one delivered delta
  Then that delta consumes exactly one sequence number and carries coalesced true with coalesced_count 50
```

## Technical notes / design
Sequence allocation is per (connection, topic) and lives beside the subscription record, incremented by the single writer task of that connection (`20-architecture.md` TG5), which makes S3 a structural property rather than a locking problem: there is exactly one writer, so there is no concurrent allocation to get wrong. The unit test named in section 16.4 ("sequence generator never skips/reuses under concurrent topic writes") therefore tests the *enqueue* side, where multiple producers converge.

Snapshot construction must not block the connection's writer task: build off the writer (in a worker or via a cached per-topic snapshot rebuilt at most once per emission tick) and hand the finished buffer to the writer. A 200-level book snapshot rebuilt per subscriber per resync storm is the obvious way to turn a small incident into an outage; the cached-snapshot-per-topic design is what bounds it.

`meta.reason` is a closed enum: `initial`, `client_resync`, `upstream_desync`, `upstream_reconnect`, `backpressure`, `reconfigure`, `instrument_revision`, `replay_seek`. `upstream_desync` and `backpressure` are **incidents** and are counted as such.

Depth-window eviction deserves care: when the top of book moves, a level that was inside the window and is now outside must be sent with size 0, otherwise the client's window silently grows stale at its edge. This is asserted directly in the unit tests.

Chunking sets `s: null` on intermediate chunks; a client that increments on a `null` sequence is broken, and the conformance suite includes a chunked snapshot precisely to catch that.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: sequence generator under concurrent enqueues from multiple topic producers; book delta application including size-0 deletes and depth-window eviction (named in section 16.4); snapshot field completeness per topic family; chunk boundary arithmetic at exactly 4 MiB, just under and just over; resync rate-limit window at the 5th and 6th request; `heatmap_bucket_selection` clamping against every row of the section 6.1.1 reference table.
- **Integration**: upstream `u` gap produces `snap` with `reason: upstream_desync` (section 16.4); recorded-fixture replay of a full symbol-day asserting that applying every delta to the snapshot reproduces the server's state byte-for-byte on OHLCV (this is R1 exit criterion 4's sibling); `snapshot: false` attach in both the provable and unprovable cases; private-topic causal ordering under a burst of fills.
- **Contract**: `snap` and `d` frames for all topics validate against sections 14-15; binary frames decode and then validate against the structured schema.
- **Perf**: full re-snapshot of the reference workspace under 700 KiB and under 400 ms (section 16.3).
- Coverage target: at least 85%.

## Security notes
Threat: **resource exhaustion via snapshot amplification** - a client that repeatedly forces re-snapshots of a 200-depth book plus a 2 000-column heatmap can consume disproportionate server CPU. Controls: the 5-per-topic-per-minute resync rate limit with revocation, the cached-snapshot-per-topic design so cost is per topic and not per subscriber, and the 2 000-column heatmap cap. Threat: **stale-data misrepresentation** - a `stale` flag that is wrong is a trading hazard; it is computed from the upstream freshness SLO and covered by an integration test with a deliberately stalled upstream. Data classification: internal for public topics, confidential for private.

## Accessibility notes
Indirect but real: the resync state drives SCR-050's "Book resynchronising..." and CMP-078's stale treatment. The `stale` flag and `meta.reason` must both be exposed to the client so the UI can distinguish "rebuilding" from "frozen" - a distinction E17-D01 established that traders need.

## Performance notes
Section 16.3: full re-snapshot of the reference workspace under 700 KiB and under 400 ms (hard fail above 2 MiB or 1.5 s); `upstream_desync` resyncs under 1 per hour per topic (hard fail above 5). Budget #6: the emit path's contribution stays inside the 20 ms backend fan-out envelope, of which the encode slice is 7 ms per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.1.

## Observability
`cv_ws_resync_total{reason}` (alert thresholds in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`), `cv_ws_snapshot_bytes{topic_family}` histogram, `cv_ws_snapshot_build_seconds{topic_family}` histogram, `cv_ws_sequence_gaps_detected_total` (must remain at zero server-side; non-zero is a bug, not a condition), `cv_ws_stale_topics` gauge. Every server-initiated resync logs `connection_id`, `ch`, `reason`, `previous_seq`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated and green.
- [ ] Recorded-fixture replay proves delta application reproduces server state exactly.
- [ ] Chunking verified above and below the 4 MiB boundary.
- [ ] Contract tests green for `snap` and `d` on every topic family in R1 scope.
- [ ] Re-snapshot size and duration budgets recorded against section 16.3.
- [ ] Coverage at least 85%.
- [ ] Metrics on E04's dashboards with the resync alert threshold wired.
- [ ] `23-ws-protocol.md` section 7 reconciled with the implementation.
- [ ] Two approvals including one code-owner.

## Dependencies

- **E17-T02** - the binary codec used to render snapshots and deltas.
- **E08** - book engine and upstream desync signals; **E12** - bar builders.
