title: Build packages/protocol WS schema extraction, codegen and the ws_message_schemas gate
body:
## Context
`23-ws-protocol.md` sections 13-15 contain **34 fenced JSON Schemas** - the control frames, the nine public payloads and the nine private payloads - and section 16.5 makes the Markdown the single source of truth: "`tools/contracts/extract_ws_schemas.py` parses every fenced json block in sections 13-15, keyed by its `$id`, and bundles them into `ws-schemas.json` - the single artefact consumed by the server (runtime response validation in dev/test), the TypeScript client codegen, and the `ws_message_schemas` gate. The Markdown is the source of truth; the bundle is always regenerated, never hand-edited."

Nothing in the rest of this Epic can be trusted without this: it is what turns "the doc says X" into "the build fails if the code does not do X", and it is the mechanism behind R1 exit criterion 7.

E02-T09 already built `packages/protocol` codegen from the OpenAPI document; this ticket adds the WS half.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tools/contracts/extract_ws_schemas.py`: parse every fenced ```json block in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` sections 13-15, key by `$id`, bundle to `packages/protocol/ws-schemas.json`. Deterministic output (sorted keys, stable formatting) so a regeneration diff is meaningful.
- `tools/contracts/validate_ws_schemas.py --draft 2020-12`: meta-validate every extracted schema, assert every `$ref` resolves **inside the bundle**, and validate **every example frame in section 12** against its declared schema. This is the blocking CI gate **`ws_message_schemas`** registered under `22-api-openapi.yaml` `x-contract-validation.gates`, running in job `contracts` / workflow `.github/workflows/contracts.yml`.
- Code generation into `packages/protocol`:
  - **Python**: `msgspec.Struct` (or pydantic v2, matching whatever E02-T09 chose for REST) models per frame type and payload, plus the topic-name and enum constants of section 6.
  - **TypeScript**: `.d.ts` types plus runtime validators for the same set, exported for `apps/web` and for `packages/chart-engine`'s feed decoder types.
- `make gen` integration and the staleness check: `make gen && git diff --exit-code` fails CI if generated output is stale (`20-architecture.md` section on tooling).
- Unit tests for the extractor itself: a schema block with a duplicate `$id` fails loudly; a block that is not valid JSON fails loudly; an added block appears in the bundle without any other edit.
- README in `packages/protocol` stating the one rule: edit the Markdown, never the bundle.

## Out of scope
- The binary codec (E17-T02) - schemas describe the *structured* form; binary/structured equivalence is asserted in E17-T02 and E17-Q01.

title: Implement the CVWB binary frame codec (header + body kinds 1-6) in Python and TypeScript
body:
## Context
The whole point of ADR-0005's data plane is that the browser can take a received `ArrayBuffer` and produce typed-array views over it with **no parse and no copy**, hand them to the GPU, and stay inside the 16.6 ms frame budget. That only works if both ends agree, byte for byte, on the fixed layout specified in `23-ws-protocol.md` section 3.4.

This ticket implements that layout once, in two languages, generated from one declaration - the mitigation ADR-0005 names for its own stated risk: "Two encodings to maintain and test. Mitigated by generating both the Python encoder and the TS decoder from a single schema declaration in `packages/protocol`, with a round-trip property test."

It is also the single largest *security* surface of the Epic: `04-security-program.md` **SR-128** requires every array length and offset to be validated on decode and forbids allocating from an untrusted length field without bounds checks, and **SR-155** requires a fuzz corpus against this decoder.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Layout declaration** in `packages/protocol` (a single data structure describing header and each body kind), from which both implementations are generated or driven.
- **Common header, 24 bytes, little-endian** exactly as section 3.4: `magic u32 = 0x43565742` ("CVWB"), `format_version u8 = 1`, `body_kind u8`, `flags u8` (bit0 estimated, bit1 coalesced, bit2 replay, bit3 partial), `price_scale u8`, `qty_scale u8`, 3 reserved zero bytes, `record_count u32`, `ts_base_ms u64`.
- **Body kinds**:
  - 1/2 book snapshot/delta - 17-byte records `{u8 side, i64 price, u64 size}`; size 0 means delete; snapshot appends a 16-byte trailer `{u64 xu, u64 xseq}`; snapshot ordering bids descending then asks ascending.
  - 3 trades - 22-byte records `{u32 ts_offset_ms, i64 price, u64 size, u8 side, u8 flags}`.
  - 4 bars - 69-byte records `{u32 ts_offset_ms, i64 o,h,l,c, u64 v, u64 turnover, u32 trades, i64 delta, u8 flags}` with bit0 `confirm`.
  - 5 footprint - per-bar group `{u32 ts_offset_ms, u32 cell_count}` then cells of 33 bytes `{i64 price, u64 bid_volume, u64 ask_volume, u32 trades, u8 flags}`.
  - 6 heatmap column - `{u32 ts_offset_ms, i64 price_min, i64 price_step, u32 row_count}` then rows of 16 bytes `{u64 bid_size, u64 ask_size}`.
- **Python encoder** (`services/api`, via `packages/protocol`): builds frames from internal event objects using scaled integers derived from the symbol's `price_scale`/`qty_scale`; zero-copy where `memoryview` allows; one encode per topic emission reused across subscribers.
- **TypeScript decoder** (`packages/protocol`, consumed by `apps/web` and `packages/chart-engine`): returns typed-array views over the received buffer without copying; validates `magic` and `format_version`; ignores trailing unknown bytes (forward compatibility, client rule C10); raises a typed `FrameMalformedError` when body length disagrees with `record_count`.
- **Structured equivalence**: a `toStructured()` path for every kind producing the section 14 schema shape, used by contract tests and by `cv.v1.json` clients (base64, `e: "b64"`).
- **Base64 wrapping** for `cv.v1.json` per section 3.2.
- **Fuzz corpus** committed under `tests/fuzz/ws-frames/` with seeds: truncated bodies, `record_count` larger than the buffer, `record_count` of 2^32-1, wrong magic, future `format_version`, negative scales, NaN-shaped bit patterns in integer fields, zero-length bodies, oversized footprint `cell_count`.

## Out of scope
- Deciding *when* to send binary vs structured (E17-S02 option handling) and *what* to send (E17-S03).
- Compression (section 3.5: deflate off for msgpack, on for JSON) - a socket-level concern configured in E17-S01.
- Snapshot chunking above 4 MiB (E17-S03) - the codec only sets and reads the `partial` flag.
- Replay clock semantics (E26); the codec only sets the `replay` flag bit.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Round trip is exact
  Given any valid internal event batch for any of the six body kinds
  When it is encoded in Python and decoded in TypeScript
  Then the decoded values equal the source exactly, including scaled integers, deletes at size 0 and every flag bit

Scenario: Binary and structured agree
  Given a frame encoded in binary and the same source encoded structured
  When both are normalised
  Then they are deeply equal, and this is asserted for all six kinds in CI

Scenario: A malformed frame never crashes and never over-allocates
  Given a frame whose record_count is 4294967295 but whose body is 32 bytes
  When the decoder runs
  Then it raises FrameMalformedError without allocating memory proportional to record_count
  And the server-side decoder equivalently rejects without panicking

Scenario: Forward compatibility
  Given a frame with 8 unknown trailing bytes after a valid body
  Then the decoder returns the valid records and ignores the trailing bytes

Scenario: Wrong magic is rejected
  Given a frame whose first four bytes are not 0x43565742
  Then the decoder raises FrameMalformedError and the client resyncs rather than rendering

Scenario: Decode stays inside budget
  Given a 50-level binary book delta and a 400-cell footprint bar
  Then decode p99 is under 0.15 ms and under 1.0 ms respectively on the reference machine
```

## Technical notes / design
All integers little-endian. Prices and sizes are **scaled 64-bit integers** using the per-symbol `price_scale`/`qty_scale` announced in the topic snapshot - never floats, never decimal strings, because both cost the render path. `ts_base_ms u64` plus `u32` per-record offsets bounds a frame's time span to ~49 days, which is far beyond any real frame and is therefore safe.

Python: `struct`/`memoryview` with pre-sized `bytearray`; avoid per-record object allocation. TypeScript: a single `DataView` for the header then `BigInt64Array`/`BigUint64Array`/`Uint32Array` subarray views for the body; note that record strides of 17, 22, 33 and 69 bytes are **not** 8-byte aligned, so typed-array views cannot be taken directly over interleaved records - decode into pre-allocated column arrays (struct-of-arrays) sized from `record_count` **after** a bounds check against the actual buffer length. That bounds check is SR-128 and is the single most important line in the file.

Error code on failure is `frame_malformed` (section 10.2), connection-scoped, closes.

Records are hard-capped before allocation: `record_count * stride + header + trailer` must equal the remaining buffer length exactly, otherwise reject. This makes over-allocation structurally impossible rather than defended against.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: per kind, encode/decode of empty, single-record, and max-size bodies; every flag bit; size-0 delete; snapshot trailer presence and absence; scale round-trip at scales 0-8; bid/ask ordering in snapshots.
- **Property (hypothesis / fast-check)**: arbitrary valid event batches round-trip Python encode to TS decode to re-encode **byte-identical** (ADR-0005's stated contract test).
- **Contract**: binary decoded then validated against the section 14 structured schema, all six kinds (section 16.4 "binary/structured equivalence").
- **Fuzz**: Atheris against the Python decoder and a JS fuzzer against the TS decoder, corpus committed, nightly 30-minute run per `04-security-program.md` section on fuzzing; a new crash blocks the next release.
- **Bench**: decode p99 per kind asserted against the section 16.3 budgets, wired as a CI benchmark.
- Coverage target: at least 85%; the decoder's error branches specifically must be covered, not just the happy path.

## Security notes
Threats: `04-security-program.md` **T-W1** ("Malformed/hostile exchange frame crashes a parser or triggers unbounded allocation") applies symmetrically to our own client-facing frames if an attacker can inject them. Controls: SR-128 bounds checking (exact-length equality before allocation), SR-155 fuzz corpus, strict magic and version checks, no dynamic allocation from untrusted lengths, typed errors instead of exceptions escaping to a generic handler. Data classification: internal (public market data). **Security review label required.**

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Budgets from section 16.3: book delta (50 levels) decode under 0.15 ms p99 (hard fail above 0.5 ms); footprint bar (400 cells) under 1.0 ms p99 (hard fail above 3 ms). Server-side encode must fit inside the 7 ms fan-out slice of budget #6's 20 ms envelope (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.1 table). Encode-once-send-many is mandatory: per-subscriber re-encoding is a defect, not an optimisation opportunity.

## Observability
`cv_ws_frame_encode_seconds{kind}` and `cv_ws_frame_bytes{kind}` histograms server-side; a client-side decode-duration mark per kind feeding the frontend performance panel.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Both implementations merged, driven from the single layout declaration.
- [ ] Round-trip property test green; binary/structured equivalence asserted for all six kinds.
- [ ] Fuzz corpus committed; nightly fuzz job wired; zero crashes.
- [ ] Decode benchmarks recorded against section 16.3 and wired into CI.
- [ ] Coverage at least 85% including error branches.
- [ ] Security engineer review recorded (SR-128, SR-155).
- [ ] `23-ws-protocol.md` section 3.4 amended if any layout detail proved wrong during implementation (spec follows reality once, deliberately, then freezes).

## Dependencies
- **E17-K01** confirms the binary data plane is the right choice before this is built.
- **E17-T01** supplies `packages/protocol` and the structured schemas the equivalence test validates against.

`feat/e17-binary-codec`

title: Implement per-topic coalescing, adaptive throttling and bounded-queue backpressure
body:
## Context
Protocol goal **G4**: "A slow or backgrounded client can never grow server memory." Architecture principle **P6** says the same thing as an absolute: bounded queues, never unbounded buffering. This task is where that property is actually implemented, and it is the difference between a self-hosted terminal that survives a laptop going to sleep and one that OOMs the backend.

It is also where *honesty under degradation* is implemented. When the server starts shedding update frequency it must say so (`connection_quality` notices on `system`, `coalesced: true` with `coalesced_count` on frames), because a tape-speed widget that silently under-reports activity during a burst is worse than one that says "feed compressed" - the trader would otherwise read a calm tape during the most violent minute of the day.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **`CoalescingQueue`** with per-family rules (section 8.2), one queue per (connection, topic):
  - `book` - per price level, last-write-wins, deletes win over earlier updates at the same level.
  - `bars` - per bar open-time, last-write-wins; **a confirmed bar is never replaced by an unconfirmed one**.
  - `footprint` - per (bar, price) cell, summed within the same bar, replaced across bars.
  - `heatmap` - per time-bucket column, last-write-wins; a whole column is dropped only if its bucket is complete and already sent.
  - `metrics` - per metric code, last point wins.
  - `ticker`, `wallet`, `positions` - whole-object last-write-wins.
  - `trades`, `liquidations` - **append, never merge**; throttling batches them into arrays.
  - `orders`, `executions` - **never coalesced, never throttled** (requirement S4).
- **Coalescing disclosure**: `coalesced: true` (structured) or header flag bit1 (binary) plus `coalesced_count`, on every merged frame.
- **Throttling**: at most one release per `throttle_ms` per topic (with `coalesce: false` a release can carry several whole frames), using the `effective` value from E17-S02, floored at `min_throttle_ms` 50 (0 only for `orders`/`executions`). Per-topic defaults from section 6.1: `book` 50 ms (depth 1 gets 20 ms, depth 200/500 get 100 ms), `trades` 100 ms, `bars` 250 ms, `footprint` 250 ms, `heatmap` equals `time_bucket_ms`, `profile` 1 000 ms, `metrics` 250 ms, `ticker.{symbol}` 250 ms, batched `ticker` 250 ms, `liquidations` 500 ms.
- **Adaptive throttling** (section 8.3): classify each connection every `CV_WS_CLASSIFY_INTERVAL_MS` (**1 000 ms** by default, 500 to 10 000; #3045) from outbound queue depth (window state included) and the RTT probe (`23-ws-protocol.md` §9.1) into `healthy` (queue under 25%, RTT under 150 ms), `lagging` (25-60% or 150-500 ms: non-critical throttles x2, force `coalesce: true`), `saturated` (60-90% or RTT over 500 ms: x4, drop `heatmap` and `profile` to 1 000 ms, emit a `system` notice), `overflowing` (over 90%: paced as `saturated` and announced; the overflow ladder runs on every push whatever the class). Class changes are **announced** on `system` as `kind: "connection_quality"` with `class`, `queue_pct`, `rtt_ms` and the `applied` block naming `throttle_multiplier`, `forced_coalesce` and `degraded_topics`.
- **Bounded outbound budget**: **8 MiB or 2 000 frames**, whichever binds first, per connection. No growth path.
- **Overflow ladder** (section 8.4), in order: (1) drop coalescable pending state for the offending topics and mark them `resnapshot_required`; (2) send `snap` with `reason: "backpressure"` for each once the queue drains below 50%; (3) if still over budget after the drop (what remains cannot be dropped: `orders`, `executions`, control or `system` frames), or after three drops in a row of one subscription's unsent `backpressure` snapshot, send `bye` with `slow_consumer` and close `4429`; (4) record `cv_ws_overflow_total{reason}` (`drop`, `unmergeable`, `resnapshot`, `close_budget`, `close_redrop`, `close_flush_deadline`) and, if step 3 fired, write a `warning` audit entry (the `ws.connection.closed` row, reason `slow_consumer`, with `after_state.trigger`).
- **`bye` hint**: the slow-consumer `bye` names `most_expensive_topics` so a reconnecting client can reduce its subscription set intelligently rather than guessing.
- **`coalesce: false` honoured only while the client keeps up**: the server re-enables coalescing under pressure and says so in the `connection_quality` notice (`applied.forced_coalesce`).

## Out of scope
- The client's side of the bargain - hidden-tab and off-screen `ctl` throttling, render decoupling (E17-T04).
- Snapshot construction and sequencing (E17-S03), though this task triggers `backpressure` re-snapshots.
- Upstream (Bybit-side) backpressure - E08.
- Tuning the `saturated` multipliers adaptively per topic cost (open item W5, deferred to the Sprint 05 load test and revisited post-R2).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Coalescing is lossless in state
  Given 500 book updates arrive for one topic within one throttle window that is already open (the first update after a quiet window leaves at once: ruling D12)
  When the coalesced frame is applied by a reference client
  Then the resulting book is identical to applying all 500 updates individually
  And the frame carries coalesced true with coalesced_count 500 and consumes exactly one sequence number

Scenario: A confirmed bar is never un-confirmed
  Given a confirmed bar for 10:05 is pending in the queue
  When an unconfirmed update for 10:05 arrives
  Then the confirmed value is kept and the unconfirmed update is discarded

Scenario: Trades are never merged
  Given 200 prints arrive within one throttle window
  Then all 200 appear in the emitted batch in order, with none dropped or summed

Scenario: Orders and executions bypass both mechanisms
  Given 50 order state transitions arrive in 100 ms
  Then 50 individual frames are emitted with no throttling and no coalescing

Scenario: Degradation is announced
  Given a connection's RTT rises above 500 ms
  Then at the first classification after the probe's age passes 500 ms (within 2 seconds at the 1 000 ms default: ruling D12) a system frame with kind connection_quality and class saturated is emitted naming the degraded topics and the applied multiplier

Scenario: A slow consumer is bounded
  Given a client stops reading for 60 seconds while subscribed to the reference workspace
  Then the connection's queued and pending bytes stay within 8 MiB and its frames within 2000 at every budget check (after each push but a non-final `snap` chunk, and after each paced update); between checks only the one chunk set being queued, or a close's `bye` and its marker, can exceed them (`23-ws-protocol.md` §8.4, §8.6). The tracemalloc peak and its ratio to the accounted bytes are recorded as evidence (ruling D8; #410 scenario 2)
  And the overflow ladder is followed in the documented order before any close
  And no other connection observes a latency regression or a sequence gap (the 60 s run and this clause: #410 scenario 2 and E17-Q03, #568)

Scenario: Undroppable topics force a close rather than a lie
  Given the outbound queue remains over budget and orders is among the affected topics
  Then bye with slow_consumer is sent, the connection closes 4429, a warning audit entry is written
  And the bye names the most expensive topics

Scenario: Recovery re-snapshots rather than replays
  Given a queue that overflowed drains below 50 percent
  Then a snap with reason backpressure is emitted for each dropped topic, and no stale queued delta is delivered
```

## Technical notes / design
Each queue is a bounded structure sized in **bytes and frames simultaneously**; the byte accounting uses the encoded length of every queued frame, and an estimate of the encoded size of each window's pending state, so the 8 MiB bound is real. State-like families store a pending *merge buffer* (a dict keyed by level/cell/bucket/metric) rather than a list of frames, which is what makes coalescing O(changes) and memory O(state) instead of O(updates).

Event-like families (`trades`, `liquidations`) store a bounded append list; if that list fills, the topic is dropped and re-snapshotted rather than silently truncated - losing prints silently would corrupt CVD and the tape.

`orders`, `executions`, `system` and every control frame are placed on a priority lane that is drained first and is never subject to the drop step (ruling D1); this is what makes step 3 of the ladder the *only* possible outcome when they are the ones backing up, and the reason the connection is closed instead: "a slow client must not be able to see a wrong position."

Classification runs in the writer's turn every `CV_WS_CLASSIFY_INTERVAL_MS` (1 000 ms by default), reading the queue accounting (window state included) and the RTT probe's sample (at most one server `ping` per classification, none while a probe is outstanding; an unanswered probe's age counts). Hysteresis: a class worsens at once and improves only after two consecutive better samples, and then to the worse of them, so a connection does not oscillate its throttles and spam `connection_quality` notices.

Config: `CV_WS_BACKPRESSURE_ENABLED` (false; C-4.13, removed with #2900), `CV_WS_QUEUE_BYTES` (8388608, lower only, floor 4194304), `CV_WS_QUEUE_FRAMES` (2000, lower only, floor 256), `CV_WS_CLASSIFY_INTERVAL_MS` (1000, 500 to 10000).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: coalescer equivalence per family - "coalescer produces state identical to applying every source update" (named in section 16.4) - as a property test over random update sequences; confirmed-bar precedence; append-never-merge for trades; byte and frame accounting at the boundary; hysteresis in classification.
- **Integration**: class transitions healthy to lagging to saturated to overflowing and back, with announcement frames asserted; overflow ladder step order; `orders` priority lane preserved while market-data topics are dropped.
- **Chaos** (feeds E17-Q02): client stops reading for 60 s - bounded memory, degradation order, `4429` (named in section 16.4); 5 000 msg/s burst on one symbol - coalescing engages, no sequence break.
- **Load** (feeds E17-Q03): 8 connections x 40 symbols for 1 h with zero resyncs attributable to backpressure.
- Coverage target: at least 85%.

## Security notes
This task **is** the availability control for the Epic's principal DoS threat: a malicious or merely broken client holding a socket open without reading. `04-security-program.md` classifies resource exhaustion as a named R1 STRIDE concern for E17 (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.4). Controls: hard byte and frame bounds with no growth path, a deterministic shed order, forced close for undroppable topics, and an audit trail for every forced close of an authenticated socket (best effort, bounded at 2 s), so repeated abuse by one identity is visible. Note the deliberate design choice: degrade **fidelity**, never **correctness** - the server drops frames and re-snapshots rather than delivering a partially applied state.

## Accessibility notes
The `connection_quality` notice drives CMP-092 and the "feed compressed" indicator designed in E17-D02. It must be announced politely (`role="status"`), not assertively - a lagging connection is not an emergency and must not interrupt a screen-reader user mid-sentence. The `degraded_topics` list must be human-readable in the UI, not raw topic strings.

## Performance notes
Budget #6: the coalescing and throttling path sits inside the 20 ms backend fan-out envelope; the merge step must be O(changes). Section 16.3: reference-workspace bandwidth under 350 KiB/s sustained (hard fail above 1 MiB/s) - throttle defaults are the primary lever. Zero resyncs from backpressure under the section 16.4 load profile is a pass condition, not an aspiration.

## Observability

Audit event: `ws.connection.closed`, reason `slow_consumer`, at warning severity; a step 3 close carries `after_state.trigger` (`budget` or `redrop`), and a close whose flush expired carries `flush_abandoned: true`.

title: Build the web WS client: reconnect, gap detection, visibility throttling and worker decode
body:
## Context
`23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.1 lists **twelve normative client obligations (C1-C12)**, and a client that ignores them can break the server's guarantees from the outside: a client that patches around a gap renders a wrong book, one that does not throttle a hidden tab wastes the whole workspace's bandwidth budget, one that renders off frame arrival instead of `requestAnimationFrame` janks under burst (section 8.5 calls this "the classic cause of jank under burst").

This task builds the single WS client used by `apps/web` and, through it, by `packages/chart-engine`'s feed decoder. It is the counterpart to E17-S01/S02/S03/T03 and the thing that makes US-MKT-005's "consumers see a brief reconnecting state rather than stale values" true on screen.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **`apps/web/src/ws/` client** with a typed API over the generated `packages/protocol` types, running its socket and binary decode in a **shared worker** so one socket serves every pane and decode never blocks the main thread (ADR-0005: decode in a worker and transfer typed arrays).
- **Handshake (C1)**: offer `cv.v1.msgpack, cv.v1.json`; send `hello` first with `client`, `client_version`, `shell` (`electron`|`browser`), `protocol`, `encodings`, `capabilities`, `locale` and `clock_ms`; send `auth` before any subscription; honour `welcome.limits` rather than hard-coding them.
- **In-place token refresh**: refresh over REST at `token_expires_at_ms - 60 s` and send a new `auth` frame on the **same** socket; never reconnect for a token refresh.
- **Per-topic sequence tracking and gap handling (C2)**: track `last_seq` per topic; on `s != last_seq + 1`, **immediately discard local state for that topic** and send `resync`; never patch around a gap; never render state assembled across one.
- **Snapshot handling (C5)**: discard prior state on every `snap` and on `ctl_ok` with `resnapshot: true`; handle chunked snapshots (`partial` flag, `s: null` on intermediate chunks).
- **Binary validation (C10)**: validate `magic` and `format_version`, ignore trailing unknown bytes, treat a body/`record_count` mismatch as `frame_malformed` and resync - delegated to E17-T02's decoder and surfaced as a typed error.
- **Reconnection (C7)**: **full-jitter** exponential backoff; do **not** auto-reconnect on `1002`, `4400` or `4403`; honour `bye.retry_after_ms`; on reconnect, re-subscribe from scratch in the priority order of section 9.3 - `system` (implicit) then private (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`) then the focused pane's topics then the other panes'.
- **Visibility and off-screen throttling (C8)**: when the Electron window or browser tab is hidden, `ctl` **all visual topics to at least 1 000 ms** and **do not unsubscribe** (unsubscribing would force a full re-snapshot on return); a pane scrolled out of view goes to 1 000 ms; a **collapsed** pane unsubscribes from its visual topics entirely.
- **Heatmap bucket derivation** (section 6.1.1): compute `time_bucket_ms` from the normative formula and ladder clamp, send it on `sub`, and re-derive on pane resize, DPR change or `window_seconds` change, sending `ctl` **debounced by 400 ms**.
- **Render decoupling (C9)**: the renderer runs off `requestAnimationFrame`; feed cadence and render cadence are independent. The client exposes a snapshot-of-latest-state read API rather than pushing per-frame callbacks into React.
- **Inbound rate discipline**: keep client-to-server frames under 30/s and 300/min excluding `pong`; batch pane-driven `ctl` calls rather than emitting one per resize event.
- **Heartbeats (C6)**: reply `pong` within 10 s of a server `ping`; send `ping` at `welcome.heartbeat.interval_ms`.
- **Unconfirmed bars (C3)**: expose `confirm` and never present `confirm: false` bars as closed to consumers.
- **Effective options (C4)**: consumers read the `effective` block, never their requested values.
- **Replay chrome (C11)** and **kill-switch/shutdown gating (C12)**: expose `source`, `rs`, `kill_switch.engaged` and `shutdown_notice` as first-class state so the UI can render distinct replay chrome and disable order-entry affordances without a REST round-trip.
- **Connection state store** feeding CMP-076/077/078/092 exactly as designed in E17-D02, including the announcement policy (assertive once per `degraded`/`offline` transition, polite for stale and for `connection_quality`).
- **Dev-only fault-injection channel** (build-flagged off in production) letting QA and design QA force each transport state deterministically.

## Out of scope
- Server behaviour (E17-S01/S02/S03/T03).
- The chart engine's rendering of the decoded arrays - `packages/chart-engine` (E11) consumes the transferred typed arrays; this task delivers them.
- Visual implementation of panes and screens beyond wiring the four connection components.
- Replay session creation and control (E26).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A gap is never patched
  Given a delta arrives with a sequence two greater than the last
  Then local state for that topic is discarded, a resync is sent, and nothing is rendered from that topic until the fresh snapshot arrives

Scenario: Hidden tab throttles but does not unsubscribe
  Given a workspace with four panes is subscribed and the tab becomes hidden
  Then every visual topic is retuned by ctl to at least 1000 ms and no unsub is sent
  And when the tab is restored no re-snapshot occurs

Scenario: Token refresh does not reconnect
  Given the access token is 60 seconds from expiry
  Then the client refreshes over REST and sends auth on the same socket
  And no snapshot is received and no subscription is recreated

Scenario: Backoff is jittered and respects fatal codes
  Given the server closes with 1011
  Then the client reconnects with full-jitter backoff
  But given a close of 4403 the client does not reconnect and routes the user to an explanatory screen

Scenario: Resubscription is prioritised
  Given a reconnect after a 30 second outage with private topics and four panes subscribed
  Then system and private topics are subscribed before the focused pane, which precedes the other panes

Scenario: Heatmap bucket is derived and debounced
  Given a heatmap pane is resized across a ladder boundary
  Then a single ctl with the newly derived time_bucket_ms is sent after a 400 ms debounce, not one per resize event

Scenario: Render is decoupled from arrival
  Given 500 frames arrive within one animation frame
  Then exactly one render occurs and no frame budget overrun is recorded

Scenario: Connection chrome matches the design
  Given each of the six transport states is forced through the fault-injection channel
  Then the chrome matches the E17-D02 artboards and each state announces per the agreed politeness exactly once per transition

Scenario: Kill-switch disables order entry without a REST call
  Given a system frame reports kill_switch engaged
  Then order-entry affordances are disabled immediately with no REST round-trip
```

## Technical notes / design
Shared worker, not a per-tab socket: `max_connections_per_user` is 8 and a four-pane workspace in three tabs would otherwise exhaust it. The worker owns the socket, the sequence table and the decoder; it posts **transferable** typed arrays to the main thread and to the engine worker, so the zero-copy property of ADR-0005 survives the hop.

State exposure follows the engine's constraint: high-frequency per-symbol state is read imperatively by the engine, not funnelled through React state, per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.1 (the frontend batching window is capped at 16 ms specifically so it never dominates latency).

Backoff: full jitter, base 500 ms, cap 30 s, reset on a successful `auth_ok` - not on socket open, since an open socket that then fails auth is not a success.

The fault-injection channel is a worker message type guarded by `import.meta.env.DEV || __CV_ALLOW_FAULT_INJECTION__`, and a build-time test asserts the production bundle does not contain it.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: sequence tracker (gap, duplicate, chunked `s: null`); backoff jitter distribution and fatal-code exclusions; visibility state machine (hidden, restored, pane collapsed, pane off-screen); heatmap bucket derivation against every row of the section 6.1.1 reference table including the clamp; `ctl` debounce and batching; token-refresh timing.
- **Contract**: the client's own frames (`hello`, `auth`, `sub`, `unsub`, `ctl`, `resync`, `ping`, `pong`) validate against the generated schemas - the client is held to the same gate as the server.
- **Integration** against a stub server implementing sections 4-9: forced snapshot, revocation, token expiry, chunked snapshot, slow-consumer close.
- **E2E (Playwright, web and Electron)**, feeding E17-Q04: hidden tab drops throttles and a restored tab does not re-snapshot (named in section 16.4); kill-switch frame disables the order ticket without a REST round-trip (named in section 16.4).
- **Perf**: decode plus state-apply stays inside the frame budget with the reference workspace under continuous feed; renderer holds 60 fps (hard fail under 45 fps p95).
- Coverage target: at least 80% (frontend floor).

## Security notes
Threats: **token handling** - the access token lives only in the worker's memory and is never placed in a URL, `localStorage` or a log; **frame trust** - every frame is treated as untrusted input and validated by the generated validators plus the binary decoder's bounds checks (SR-128); **fault-injection channel** - must be absent from production bundles, asserted by a build test; **error disclosure** - `request_id` and `connection_id` are shown only behind a "copy details" affordance, never in default copy.

## Accessibility notes
Binding, and implemented exactly as signed off in E17-D02: CMP-076 announces `degraded`/`offline` assertively once per transition and never per heartbeat; CMP-077 is `role="alertdialog"` with a focus trap and a keyboard-operable retry; CMP-078 renders a visible "Last update Xs ago" alongside the shading; CMP-092 uses `role="status"` or `role="alert"` by severity with per-issue dismissal that reappears while the condition persists. `prefers-reduced-motion` disables the reconnect animation. axe-core must be clean on SCR-152 in every state.

## Performance notes
Section 16.3: end-to-end tick-to-pixel under 40 ms p95 locally (hard fail above 120 ms); renderer 60 fps under continuous feed (hard fail under 45 fps p95); decode budgets per E17-T02. Budget #3: WS tick to screen p95 under 100 ms, p99 under 250 ms. The client's batching window is capped at one frame (16 ms) by design.

## Observability
Client-side marks per stage (`ws.receive`, `ws.decode`, `state.apply`, `paint`) exported through E04's frontend performance channel so budget #3 is measured end to end with the backend span id carried on the envelope. Counters for local gap detections, resyncs sent, reconnect attempts and forced re-snapshots, surfaced in the diagnostics bundle (E04-S02).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All twelve client obligations C1-C12 implemented and each covered by at least one test.
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated and green.
- [ ] Contract tests green on client-emitted frames.
- [ ] Coverage at least 80%; axe-core clean on SCR-152 in every state.
- [ ] Fault-injection channel present in dev, proven absent from the production bundle.
- [ ] Budget #3 and the section 16.3 client budgets measured and recorded.
- [ ] Design QA (E17-D04) passed.
- [ ] Two approvals including one code-owner.

## Dependencies

- **E17-T02** - the TypeScript decoder.
- **E17-D02** - signed-off designs, copy deck and announcement policy (design-ahead rule).

title: Generate the single-source error registry and wire the error_registry_single_source gate
body:
## Context
`23-ws-protocol.md` section 10.2 is emphatic that its 28-code error table is **not** an independently maintained list: it is "a rendering of a partition of the one product-wide error registry" that lives in `22-api-openapi.yaml` under `x-error-codes` (six of which are dual-surface: `forbidden`, `account_scope_denied`, `no_data_recorded`, `degraded_data`, `exchange_unavailable`, `internal_error`) and `x-error-codes-ws` (WS-only transport codes, each carrying a `rest_analogue`).

The reason is practical: the web client keeps **one** error-mapping table for both surfaces (section 10.3 maps codes to UI treatment classes), and that only works if a code means the same thing wherever it appears. Without the gate, the two documents drift within a sprint and the client's mapping silently develops holes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tools/errorcodes/generate.py`: read `x-error-codes` and `x-error-codes-ws` from `22-api-openapi.yaml` and emit `services/api/app/errors/error_codes.py` and `packages/protocol/src/errorCodes.ts` - enums plus per-code metadata (`scope`, `retryable`, `rest_analogue`, close-code association where applicable).
- `tools/contracts/check_error_registry.py` implementing the blocking gate **`error_registry_single_source`**, asserting: (a) the Code column of `23-ws-protocol.md` section 10.2 equals exactly the union of `x-error-codes-ws` and the `surface: [rest, ws]` subset of `x-error-codes` - no extras, no omissions; (b) every `rest_analogue` value resolves to a real REST code; (c) the generated enums are byte-identical to a fresh regeneration.
- Registration in the `contracts` CI job (`.github/workflows/contracts.yml`) and in `make contracts` for offline local running.
- A **runtime assertion** in the WS gateway's error path: emitting a code absent from the generated enum raises in dev and test builds, which is how requirement **S10** ("emit only error codes from the section 10.2 catalogue") becomes enforceable rather than aspirational.
- Client-side mapping table in `apps/web` driven by the generated metadata and the section 10.3 UI classes: fatal (modal, route to login), transient self-healing (inline staleness badge plus connection chip, no modal), client bug (console error plus a report-a-bug toast, never a silent swallow), capacity (toast advising fewer panes, auto-reduce throttles).

## Out of scope
- Adding or changing any error code's semantics - this task mechanises what exists.
- REST error handling (E02/E09 already own the `problem+json` path).
- The WS schema bundle (E17-T01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The registry is single-source
  When error_registry_single_source runs
  Then the section 10.2 code column equals the union of the two registry blocks exactly

Scenario: Adding a code in one place fails the build
  Given a developer adds a WS error code to 23-ws-protocol.md section 10.2 but not to 22-api-openapi.yaml
  When CI runs
  Then the gate fails naming the orphan code, and the reverse case fails likewise

Scenario: Generated enums cannot drift
  Given a developer hand-edits errorCodes.ts
  Then the gate fails because regeneration is not byte-identical

Scenario: A dangling rest_analogue is caught
  Given a WS code declares a rest_analogue that no REST code defines
  Then the gate fails naming both

Scenario: An undocumented code can never be emitted
  Given the gateway attempts to emit an error code not in the generated enum
  Then in dev and test builds it raises, and a test asserts this
```

## Technical notes / design
The section 10.2 table is parsed from the Markdown by column position with a strict parser - a malformed table row fails the gate rather than being skipped, because a silently skipped row is exactly the drift the gate exists to prevent.

Generated files carry a do-not-edit header naming the generator and the source document. Both generated artefacts are committed so the staleness check (`make gen && git diff --exit-code`) covers them.

body:
## Context
`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budget #6 - backend fan-out add-on at most 20 ms p95, measured from book update to outbound WS frame emitted - is a **hard** gate, and budget #3 (WS tick to screen, p95 under 100 ms) can only be measured end to end if the backend span id is propagated to the frontend **via the WS message envelope**. Section 7.2 of that document calls this out as "a specific architecture requirement, not just have logs on both sides".

Separately, `23-ws-protocol.md` attaches alert-worthy semantics to two counters: `cv_ws_resync_total{reason}` (upstream_desync and backpressure are incidents with alert thresholds) and `cv_ws_overflow_total{reason}`. Without them, a degrading connection is invisible until a user complains.

E04 built the metrics facade, correlation-id propagation and the dashboards; this task populates them for M23.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Metrics** registered through E04's facade:
  - `cv_ws_clients` (gauge), `cv_ws_topics_per_client` (gauge, per `20-architecture.md` capacity table).
  - `cv_ws_resync_total{reason}` over the closed reason enum; `cv_ws_overflow_total{reason}`; `cv_ws_conflated_total{topic_family}`.
  - `cv_ws_frame_encode_seconds{kind}`, `cv_ws_frame_bytes{kind}`, `cv_ws_snapshot_build_seconds{topic_family}`, `cv_ws_snapshot_bytes{topic_family}`.
  - `cv_ws_fanout_seconds` histogram - **the budget #6 measurement**: bus event received to outbound frame handed to the socket.
  - `cv_ws_connection_class{class}` gauge, `cv_ws_queue_bytes`, `cv_ws_queue_frames`, `cv_ws_rtt_seconds`, and the `cv_ws_coalesced_count` histogram (from E17-T03, ruling D6), aggregated per process.
  - `cv_ws_errors_total{code}` (bounded cardinality 28, from E17-T05's closed catalogue), `cv_ws_auth_failures_total{reason}`, `cv_ws_revoked_total{reason}`, `cv_ws_closes_total{reason}` (§8: `reason` alone), `cv_ws_clock_skew_ms`.
- **Cross-stack trace correlation**: carry the backend span id on the frame envelope so a single tick correlates from Bybit ingestion through fan-out to frontend paint, satisfying section 7.2's requirement. The envelope field is additive and therefore does not bump `cv.v1` (section 2.3).
- **Structured logs** with E04's correlation id on every connection lifecycle event, every server-initiated resync (`ch`, `reason`, `previous_seq`), every overflow action and every close, at the severities agreed with E04.
- **Grafana panel additions** to E04's existing dashboards: a WS row with connection count, class distribution, fan-out p95 against the 20 ms line, resync rate per reason against the under-1-per-hour-per-topic threshold, overflow actions, bandwidth per connection.
- **Alerts** via E04's two-severity Alertmanager rule set: fan-out p95 over budget for 5 minutes (warning); `upstream_desync` resyncs above 5 per hour per topic (warning, per section 16.3's hard-fail line); any `slow_consumer` close (warning, since it implies a user lost their feed); `cv_ws_sequence_gaps_detected_total` above zero (critical - a server-side gap is a correctness bug, not a condition).
- **Runbook** entries for each alert in the E04 runbook format: what it means, what to check first, what action to take.

## Out of scope
- The observability platform itself - E04 owns Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, structlog and the diagnostics bundle.
- Frontend performance marks - E17-T04 emits those; this task only guarantees the correlating span id is on the wire.
- Load testing - E17-Q03.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budget #6 is measurable, not asserted
  Given the gateway is serving the reference workspace
  Then cv_ws_fanout_seconds is populated and its p95 is visible on the dashboard against the 20 ms budget line

Scenario: A single tick correlates end to end
  Given a book update from Bybit ingestion
  Then the backend span id appears on the outbound envelope and the frontend performance mark carries the same id, so the full path is one trace

Scenario: Resync incidents alert
  Given upstream_desync resyncs exceed 5 per hour on one topic
  Then a warning alert fires with a runbook link

Scenario: Label cardinality stays bounded
  Given a full day of traffic
  Then no WS metric exceeds its documented label cardinality, and no metric carries a symbol or user id as an unbounded label

Scenario: A server-side sequence gap is treated as a bug
  Given cv_ws_sequence_gaps_detected_total increments
  Then a critical alert fires, because the server guarantees it cannot happen
```

## Technical notes / design
Cardinality discipline matters more than usual here: `topic_family` (11 public plus 9 private) and `kind` (6) are safe labels; **symbol and user id are not** and must stay out of labels - they belong in logs and in exemplars. `cv_ws_topics_per_client` is a gauge summarised per connection, not a per-topic series.

The fan-out histogram brackets exactly the span budget #6 defines - bus receipt to frame handed to the socket - excluding the client's network time, so a slow Tailscale link never flatters or condemns the backend number.

Instrumentation must not itself cost the budget: E04-K01 measured the facade's overhead; keep the hot path to counter increments and one histogram observation per emitted frame, with no string formatting.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: every metric registered exactly once; label sets fixed; the fan-out timer brackets the intended span.

- **Perf**: instrumentation overhead under 2% of the fan-out path, measured against an uninstrumented build.
- **Ops**: each alert fired once in staging by injecting its condition, and its runbook followed end to end.
- Coverage target: at least 85%.

Logs and metrics must never contain an access token, an API key, a raw account identifier in a metric label, or a user's personal data. N/A (operator-facing; the Grafana panels follow E04's already-reviewed dashboard conventions).

Instrumentation overhead at most 2% of the fan-out path. The measurement itself is the enforcement mechanism for budget #6 (hard) and the input to budget #3 (hard at R2 exit, measured a train early per R1 exit criterion 3).

This ticket is observability. Its own success criterion is that budgets #3 and #6 can be read off a dashboard without ad hoc instrumentation during the R1 PRR.

title: Freeze the protocol: reconcile 23-ws-protocol.md, amend ADR-0005 and add the breaking-change gate
body:
## Context
R1 exit criterion 7 (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.3): "**WS protocol is frozen**: `23-ws-protocol.md` matches the implementation, contract tests pass, and a deliberate breaking change fails CI." R1 goal 4 gives the reason: R2 and R3 must be able to *add topics* without renegotiating transport, which is only true if the transport is settled and mechanically protected.

Implementation always teaches the spec something. This ticket is the deliberate, **one-time** reconciliation where the document is corrected to match reality, after which the direction of travel reverses permanently: from then on, code moves to match the spec (`runtime_spec_parity` gate: "spec is the source of truth; code moves to match").

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Reconciliation pass** over `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` against the shipped implementation, section by section: 2 (negotiation), 3 (framing and binary layout), 4 (lifecycle, close codes), 5 (sub/unsub/ctl), 6 (topic catalogue, options, defaults, permission matrix), 7 (snapshot, delta, resync reasons), 8 (coalescing rules, classes, overflow ladder), 9 (heartbeats, resubscription, revocation), 10 (error catalogue), 16.2 (limits). Every divergence is resolved explicitly: either the document is corrected, or a defect is filed against the implementation. **No divergence may be left undocumented.**
- **Close the open items** in section 16.6: **W1** (measured bandwidth and CPU, from E17-K01), **W2** (depth 500 keep-or-drop, from E17-K01), **W5** (per-topic coalescing thresholds under `saturated`, from E17-Q03's load results). W3 is already closed; W4 (session resumption) stays deferred with a restated rationale and a post-R2 review date.
- **Amend ADR-0005** with the measured numbers from E17-K01 and an explicit statement of whether its validation gate was met, plus any layout corrections from E17-T02 and a note on what the implementation taught.
- **The breaking-change CI gate**: a test that pins the wire contract - the binary header layout and every body-kind record stride, the control-frame required-field sets, the close-code set and the error-code set - against a committed golden fixture. Changing any of them fails CI with a message explaining that a breaking change requires `cv.v2` served in parallel for at least one release (section 2.3). The gate must be demonstrated failing on a deliberate break during review.
- **`runtime_spec_parity`** wired for the WS surface: the running server's advertised `welcome.limits`, topic catalogue and error catalogue are compared against the document, so a limit changed in config without a doc change fails the build.
- **Additive-change guidance** documented in `packages/protocol/README.md`: what is additive and therefore free (new topic, new optional field, new error code - clients must ignore unknown fields and topics) versus what requires `cv.v2`.
- **Update `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`** SCR-152 and the section 0.5.4 invariant if the shipped behaviour diverged, and `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 3.12 if the component decomposition diverged.

## Out of scope
- New protocol features - the point of the ticket is that there are none.
- E26's replay routing, which adds no new framing.
- Re-running the load tests (E17-Q03 owns them; this ticket consumes their numbers).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The document matches the implementation
  When each section of 23-ws-protocol.md is walked against the shipped code
  Then every divergence is either corrected in the document or filed as a defect, and the reconciliation table on this ticket lists all of them

Scenario: Config drift is caught

  Then runtime_spec_parity fails

Scenario: Open items are closed with evidence
  Then section 16.6 marks W1, W2 and W5 resolved, each citing the ticket and the measured numbers that resolved it
```

## Technical notes / design
The golden fixture is a committed JSON description of the wire contract - not a prose assertion - generated once from the implementation at freeze time and thereafter compared: `{header: {size, fields}, body_kinds: {1..6: {stride, fields}}, control_frames: {name: required_fields}, close_codes: [...], error_codes: [...], limits: {...}}`. Regenerating it is a deliberate act that shows up as a reviewable diff in a PR that must also explain itself, which is exactly the friction the freeze is meant to create.

The reconciliation table lives on this ticket and in the PR description: one row per divergence with section, what the doc said, what the code did, and the resolution. Reviewers check the table, not just the diff.

## Test plan
- The wire-contract gate is itself the test; it is demonstrated failing on a deliberate break (stride change, removed required field, removed error code) and passing on an additive change.
- `runtime_spec_parity` exercised against a running instance in the docker-compose test environment.
- No new functional tests - if reconciliation reveals behaviour without a test, that is a defect filed against the owning story, not patched here.

## Security notes
The freeze is itself a security control: a pinned, reviewed wire contract means a decoder-affecting change cannot land without deliberate review, which is the structural half of the mitigation for `04-security-program.md` T-W1 (malformed frame handling) - the other half being E17-T02's bounds checks and fuzzing.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Section 16.3's budget table is restated from measured values (E17-K01, E17-Q03) rather than left as engineering estimates - this is the substantive part of closing W1.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Reconciliation table complete; every divergence resolved or filed.
- [ ] `23-ws-protocol.md` merged in its reconciled form; section 16.6 W1, W2, W5 closed with evidence; W4 restated as deferred.
- [ ] ADR-0005 amended with measured numbers and a gate met/not-met statement.

body:
## Context
`04-security-program.md` section 5 requires a STRIDE model per epic ("Every area is re-reviewed when its epic enters design"), `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.1 makes the kickoff a DoR item, and `30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.4 names the three concerns for E17 specifically: **WS auth, topic authorization, resource exhaustion**.

E17 deserves a careful model rather than a checkbox because it is the component where three security-relevant things meet: an **unauthenticated socket exists for up to 10 seconds by design** (browser WebSockets cannot carry headers, so auth is a first frame - section 4.3); **authorisation is evaluated continuously rather than once**, since grants can change mid-connection; and the server **deliberately holds per-connection state and queues**, which is exactly the shape an attacker exploits for resource exhaustion.

It is also the component through which a hostile or corrupt frame reaches a **binary decoder** on both ends - `04-security-program.md` threat **T-W1** ("Malformed/hostile exchange frame crashes a parser or triggers unbounded allocation") applies to our own client-facing framing, not only to the exchange's.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Data-flow diagram** of the gateway with trust boundaries drawn explicitly: untrusted client socket to `Handshake`; `Handshake` to E09 auth/RBAC; internal bus to `FeedMultiplexer`; `CoalescingQueue` to `FrameEncoder` to socket; the upstream ingestion boundary; and the browser-side worker/main boundary in `apps/web`.
- **STRIDE analysis per element and per flow**, in the table format of `04-security-program.md` section 5 (`T` id, STRIDE category, threat, likelihood, impact, risk, mitigating requirements, residual), covering at minimum:
  - **Spoofing** - token replay on a new socket; a stolen token used from another host; the 10 s unauthenticated window; `hello` impersonating another client build.
  - **Tampering** - hostile binary body (unbounded `record_count`, truncated body, wrong magic); option injection through unknown keys; topic-name injection attempting to escape the registry; envelope field injection.
  - **Repudiation** - a subscription to a private topic without an audit trail; a revocation that leaves no record.
  - **Information disclosure** - token in a URL, log, metric label or error message; cross-account data leaking through scope narrowing; differential error messages revealing which accounts exist; `connection_id`/`git_sha`/`request_id` exposure to a Viewer; `system` topic content not filtered by role.
  - **Denial of service** - slow consumer growing server memory; resync loop forcing snapshot rebuilds; subscription and symbol exhaustion; inbound frame flood; oversized inbound frame; connection exhaustion per user; expensive-topic amplification (200-depth book plus 2 000-column heatmap).
  - **Elevation of privilege** - subscribing to another account's private topics by raw frame; a stale permission set surviving a grant change; a `replay_session_id` reaching a private topic; kill-switch state not honoured.
- **Mapping each threat to its mitigating requirement** in `04-security-program.md` (notably **SR-040** strict schema plus size caps, **SR-128** bounds-checked binary decode, **SR-155** fuzzed decoders) and to the E17 ticket that implements it, so no threat is left with an unassigned control.
- **Residual risk statement** per threat, with Owner sign-off on anything accepted rather than mitigated.
- **Findings appended to `04-security-program.md` section 5** as a new area block (SR-157: per-epic output is appended, not kept in a side document).
- **Abuse-case seeds** handed to E17-X02 for adversarial testing.
- **Risk register update** (`32-risk-register.md`) for R3 (real-time cost) and any new entry the model surfaces.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the controls - they belong to E17-S01/S02/S03/T02/T03.
- Executing the adversarial tests (E17-X02).
- The auth and RBAC systems themselves (E09's own model); this model consumes them and asserts the boundary is used correctly.
- Upstream Bybit connection security (E08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every STRIDE category is addressed
  When the model is reviewed
  Then all six categories have at least one analysed threat or an explicit, reasoned out-of-band statement

Scenario: Every threat has an owner and a control
  Then each threat names a mitigating requirement and the E17 ticket implementing it, or is explicitly accepted with Owner sign-off

Scenario: The three named R1 concerns are covered in depth
  Then WS auth, topic authorization and resource exhaustion each have a dedicated analysis section rather than a single row

Scenario: A gap becomes work
  Given the model finds a threat with no implementing control
  Then a ticket is filed against the appropriate E17 story in the same sprint, not deferred to a backlog note

Scenario: The model is recorded where the programme expects it
  Then the findings are appended to 04-security-program.md section 5 as an E17 area block and referenced from this ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
Two analyses deserve more than a table row and should be written out as short narratives:

**The 10-second unauthenticated window.** It cannot be removed (browser WebSockets cannot set headers, and a query-string token is worse - it lands in proxy logs and browser history). The model must therefore argue the window is *bounded and cheap*: 10 s timeout, 3 auth attempts, 8 connections per user, inbound rate limiting applied **before** auth as well as after, and no per-connection allocation beyond the socket until `auth_ok`. The residual risk is connection-slot exhaustion by an unauthenticated attacker who can reach the port - which Tailscale-only exposure reduces to "someone already on the tailnet", and that should be stated rather than assumed.

**Continuous authorisation.** A permission check at subscribe time is necessary but not sufficient, because a subscription can outlive the grant that justified it. The model must show that the revocation path (E17-S02's reverse index plus E09's grant-change events) has no gap in which data for a withdrawn account can still be emitted, and must consider the reconnect race that E17-Q02 tests.

## Test plan
The model produces the abuse cases E17-X02 executes; it is not itself a test. Its own review criterion: a second reviewer (Architect) attempts to name a threat the model missed, and either fails or the model is amended.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security deliverable. Data classification recorded per flow: public market-data topics are **internal**; private topics (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`, `trade_groups`) are **confidential** and account-scoped; the `auth_ok` payload is confidential (it enumerates the user's account scope); tokens are **secret**.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Several controls are also performance limits (subscription caps, queue bounds, resync rate limits). The model must state where a security limit and a performance budget are the same number, so neither is relaxed in isolation for the other's reasons - loosening the 8 MiB queue to help a slow link would silently remove a DoS control.

## Observability
The model specifies which threats must be **detectable**, not merely prevented: repeated `auth_failed` per identity, slow-consumer closes per identity, resync-rate-limit revocations, and denied cross-account subscribes - each with an audit event and a metric so abuse is visible rather than merely blocked.

title: Security review, abuse cases, decoder fuzzing and SAST/DAST rules for the WS surface
body:
## Context
E17-X01 produces the model; this ticket **tests it adversarially** and leaves behind automation so the same holes cannot reopen. `23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.4 names four security rows outright:

- Token in a query string is rejected; an expired token closes `4401`.
- A manager cannot subscribe to another manager's accounts, **even by raw frame**.
- Fuzzed binary bodies never panic the server or the client decoder.

and `04-security-program.md` **SR-155** requires fuzz tests against "the exchange-message decoders, the client WS binary framing decoder and the rule IR parser, with a corpus committed and a nightly longer run".

The distinction from E17-Q01 is deliberate: QA tests that the system does what it should; this ticket tests that it refuses what it must.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Abuse-case test suite** (`tests/security/ws/`), derived from E17-X01's seeds, driven by a **raw protocol client that ignores all client-side rules** - because the real attacker will:
  - Token in the query string, token in `hello`, token in a topic option - all must be ignored and the auth window must still time out.
  - Expired, tampered-signature, wrong-audience and revoked-session tokens - all close `4401`.
  - A manager raw-frame subscribing to `positions`, `orders`, `executions`, `wallet` and `trade_groups` for an account outside scope - all `account_scope_denied`, with **no data ever emitted** for that account.
  - A Viewer attempting anything mutating - refused server-side (mutations are REST; the WS must not offer a side door).
  - Probing for account existence through differential error messages and timing - must be indistinguishable.
  - `replay_session_id` on a private topic - `invalid_options`.
  - Topic-name injection: path-like names, unicode homoglyph symbols, extremely long names, null bytes, names with embedded dots in `param` - all rejected by the registry, never reaching a producer.
  - Option smuggling: unknown keys, out-of-range values, negative throttles, `symbols` lists above 40, deeply nested option objects.
  - Resource exhaustion: subscription flood to the 200 cap, symbol flood to the 40 cap, connection flood past 8 per user, resync loop past 5/min/topic, 256 KiB-plus inbound frames, inbound frame flood past 30/s - each must be refused with the documented code and must not degrade another user.
  - A stale permission set: grant withdrawn, then a frame in flight for the withdrawn account - must not be emitted.
- **Fuzzing** (SR-155): **Atheris** against the Python frame decoder and option parser; a JS fuzzer against the TypeScript binary decoder; corpus committed at `tests/fuzz/ws-frames/` and seeded from E17-T02's seeds plus mutations of recorded valid frames. Wired as a **nightly 30-minute run**; any new crash blocks the next release (`04-security-program.md` fuzzing table).
- **SAST rules**: Semgrep/Bandit rules specific to this surface - forbid constructing an error frame outside the `raise_ws_error` helper (so the closed catalogue holds), forbid allocating from a decoded length field without a preceding bounds check (SR-128), forbid logging any variable named like a token or an authorization header, forbid a permission check performed anywhere but the RBAC service.
- **DAST**: an OWASP ZAP (or equivalent WS-capable) pass against the WS endpoint in staging, covering handshake manipulation, origin checks, TLS configuration and subprotocol confusion.
- **Security review** of the E17 code: the auth path, the authorisation path, the decoder and the queue accounting, reviewed line by line by the Security engineer against the model's controls.
- **Findings** triaged, fixed or accepted with Owner sign-off, and the model updated where reality diverged.

## Out of scope
- The pen-test itself - scheduled before R4 Live enablement (E43), not here.
- Auth and RBAC internals (E09's own security tickets).
- Rule IR fuzzing (E35), exchange-decoder fuzzing (E08) - SR-155's other two targets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No token path other than the auth frame works
  Given a token supplied in the query string, in hello and in a topic option
  Then none authenticates the connection and the auth timeout fires with close 4401

Scenario: Cross-account access is impossible by raw frame
  Given a manager scoped to account A crafts frames for account B across every private topic
  Then every attempt is refused with account_scope_denied and no frame for account B is ever emitted on that connection

Scenario: Account existence cannot be probed
  Given subscribe attempts for an existing out-of-scope account and for a non-existent account
  Then the error code, message and response timing are indistinguishable

Scenario: Fuzzing finds no crash
  Given a 30 minute Atheris run against the Python decoder and an equivalent JS run against the TypeScript decoder
  Then no crash, hang or unbounded allocation occurs, and the corpus is committed

Scenario: A regression is caught by the rules
  Given a developer adds code allocating a list sized from a decoded record_count without a bounds check
  Then the SAST rule fails the build citing SR-128

Scenario: Resource limits hold under abuse
  Given a client floods subscriptions, symbols, connections, resyncs and inbound frames simultaneously
  Then each is refused with its documented error code, the connection is closed where documented
  And a concurrently connected legitimate user observes no latency regression

Scenario: Findings are closed
  Then every finding is fixed or accepted with Owner sign-off, and the security review comment is recorded on the Epic
```

## Technical notes / design
The abuse client deliberately shares **no** code with `apps/web`'s client, only the generated types - otherwise the client's own guardrails would be doing the refusing and the server would never be tested. This is the single most important design decision in the ticket.

Timing indistinguishability is measured statistically, not asserted by eyeball: a few hundred samples of each error path with overlapping distributions. Constant-time comparison is not required for the topic registry, but the *code path length* must not differ meaningfully between "account exists but is out of scope" and "account does not exist" - both resolve through the same scope intersection.

Fuzz seeds beyond E17-T02's: valid frames with a single bit flipped at every offset of the header; valid frames truncated at every byte boundary; `record_count` set to each power of two; nested MessagePack maps at depth 100; a 256 KiB frame of random bytes with a valid magic.

## Test plan
This ticket is a test deliverable. All abuse cases run in the `security` CI job; the fuzz job runs nightly for 30 minutes with a longer weekend run. A new fuzz crash opens a P0 bug automatically per the fuzzing policy.

## Security notes
The whole ticket. Controls verified: SR-040 (strict schema plus size caps), SR-128 (bounds-checked decode), SR-155 (fuzzing with committed corpus), plus the topic-permission matrix and account-scope narrowing of `23-ws-protocol.md` section 6.3. Threats from E17-X01's model are each mapped to at least one executed abuse case; any threat without one is a gap in this ticket, not in the model. Testing runs against staging with fixture data and provisioned test identities - **never** against live accounts or real API keys.

## Accessibility notes
One accessibility-adjacent security check: error copy shown to a Viewer must not leak `request_id`, `connection_id` or `git_sha` in the default rendering, and the "copy details" affordance that does expose them must itself be keyboard-reachable and labelled.

## Performance notes
The resource-exhaustion abuse cases assert the security limits and the performance budgets together: while a client floods, a concurrently connected legitimate user's fan-out p95 must stay inside budget #6. A control that protects memory but destroys latency has not worked.

## Observability
Verify that each refused abuse emits its audit event and increments its metric - `cv_ws_auth_failures_total`, `cv_ws_errors_total{code}`, `cv_ws_revoked_total{reason}`, `cv_ws_closes_total{reason}`. A silently refused attack is a detection failure even though it is a prevention success.

- [ ] Abuse-case suite implemented, green, and mapped one-to-one against E17-X01's threats.

- [ ] SAST rules merged and each demonstrated failing on a deliberate violation.

title: Statechart-backed WS topic: machines.{entity}.state (state/enum, snapshot+delta, per-entity RBAC)
body:
## Context
Every catalogue lifecycle B1-B20 (`28-statechart-catalogue.md`) is built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1` from its first line of code (ADR-0016 Accepted, `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §4d). The UI needs to see machine state without ever querying the interpreter on the hot path (MUSTNOT-03): `machines.{entity}.state` is a dedicated WS topic, built on the E17 subscription/topic-registry and snapshot+delta machinery already implemented by E17-S02/E17-S03, fed by the `CvMetricsPlugin`/`CvAuditPlugin` on_transition hooks landed in E50-T60 rather than by polling any `Interpreter` instance.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Register `machines.{entity}.state` in the E17-S02 topic registry: `entity` is the catalogue machine's public id (e.g. `order:{order_id}`, `session:{session_id}`, `kill_switch`, `risk_lockout:{account_id}`).
- On every interpreter transition, `CvMetricsPlugin`'s `on_transition` hook (E50-T60) publishes `{state: <published enum>, context_summary: <redacted>, machine_hash}` onto the topic; the WS server never calls into `statechart/factory.py` or holds an `Interpreter` reference to answer a client query.
- Snapshot: on subscribe, the current published state is served as an E17-S03 snapshot frame; subsequent transitions are E17-S03 delta frames on the same sequence numbering as every other topic (no bespoke resync path for statechart topics).
- Per-entity RBAC: subscription is authorised per the E17-S02 topic-registry rule set against the entity owner/account scope (a manager cannot subscribe to another account's `risk_lockout` topic).
- Coalescing/backpressure/throttling for this topic reuse E17-T03 unchanged; a burst of rapid transitions (e.g. a chain of `after:` timers) is coalesced to the latest state, never buffered unboundedly.

## Out of scope
- The admin statechart inspector screen and its read API - **E42-T07**/**E42-S08**; this task is the live-update topic only, not the historical/list view.
- Building or hashing any individual `machine.json` - **E50-S01**/**E50-S02**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Subscribe to a machine's live state
  Given I hold a valid subscription to machines.order:o123.state
  When the order's B1 machine transitions
  Then I receive a delta frame with the new published state within one coalescing window

Scenario: No interpreter query on the hot path
  Given the WS server publishes a state update
  Then it is sourced entirely from the on_transition hook payload, with no call into factory.py, persistence.py or any Interpreter instance

Scenario: RBAC blocks cross-account subscription
  Given I am a manager on account A
  When I attempt to subscribe to machines.risk_lockout:B.state for account B
  Then the subscription is refused
```

## Technical notes / design
This topic is a thin publisher over the existing E17 transport; it holds no statechart import (`CV-LINT-IMPORT` applies transitively - this module is outside the whitelisted pair). The `machine_hash` is included on every frame so a client can detect it is running against a stale contract build. Built directly on the library via the factory/plugin surface: no hand-rolled state machine, no enum+transition table, no shim, no dual-runtime.

## Test plan
Contract: subscribe/snapshot/delta frame shapes against `23-ws-protocol.md` plus the `machine_hash` field. Integration: transition burst -> coalesced delta, cross-account RBAC refusal, resubscribe mid-chain of `after:` timers.
